The ad presents True Effect as the solution, highlighting higher attribution conversions, user-centric audience views, broader customer targeting, and cross-device user stitching for more accurate measurement. The ad encourages viewers to contact True Effect and is aimed at advertisers.

An advertisment for 4imprint shows blue text against a white background asking 'Why 4imprint?' as a voice over says that the art team at 4imprint takes its job seriously. Footage is shown of a man running over to a computer and being surrounded by his co-workers, as he sweats and trembles while using a computer program to align a graphic logo onto a hat. The co-workers cheer as the man puts the hat on. The ad promotes a hardworking company in an upbeat tone.

An advertisement for Mirinda soda shows a boy playing the video game 'The Legend of Zelda'.  In the game, Link opens a treasure chest filled with Mirinda soda and begins drinking it without stopping and ignoring the boy. The boy tries to get control of Link by shaking the controller, waiting, and eventually shaking the TV while Link continues to ignore him. A younger child watches this unfold while holding a Mirinda soda. The ad suggests the soda's obsessive appeal in a humorous way.

An advertisement for Join or Die with Craig Ferguson shows a montage of clips of host Craig Ferguson speaking to celebrities, journalists, and scholars about history in a comedic way. The people make jokes, laugh, and debate in a television studio in front of an audience, intercut with footage of Craig Ferguson sitting on a couch while talking to the camera about the show. The ad end with logos and graphics, and a shorter teaser of Craig Ferguson talking to the camera. The ad is presented in a humorous and informative tone for audiences that enjoy satirical comedy.

An advertisement for the Volkswagen Beetle car shows a CGI forest full of insects walking around, when suddenly a black beetle races past and energetic rock music plays. Other insects stop and look as the beetle zooms past them - skidding, jumping, and turning corners like a car would - before stopping on a rock where the silhouette of the beetle turns into a graphic of a Volkswagen Beetle car with relevant text branding. The ad promotes Volkswagen as fast and stylish with a humorous and energetic tone.

An advertisement for The Legend of Zelda: Twilight Princess for the Wii U features a series of cutscenes and gameplay footage set to orchestral music. The main character, Link, explores the game world and battles monsters. The video highlights gameplay mechanics such as Hero Mode, the Ghost Lantern, and the Wolf Link Amiibo. The game is presented as being available on March 4, 2016 for the Wii U system and is targeted at gamers.

An advertisement for Vice Sports Shorts featuring a preview of a short for Karl Anthony Towns training for the NBA. The ad features key shots include Karl doing agility training, jumps, squats and battle ropes in the gym and on court training shots with his father coaching him to sharpen his shooting skills. It highlights how much time and training is required, showing his development, and ending with the Gatorade logo.

An advertisement for MasterCard shows Peyton Manning yelling while grilling in a parking lot as people walk past with quizzical expressions and a voice over and text graphic state the price of the grill. Next, Manning is shown yelling while ordering a sandwich and then putting gas with matching voice over and text. Lastly, Manning yells are strangers on a staircase and gets a high five as the voice over says, 'fans = priceless', and company branding is shown. The ad promotes MasterCard as a valuable product, much like fans are to Peyton Manning, and is presented in a humorous tone.

An advertisement for Pokémon Blue Version shows gameplay footage of a player exploring a monochrome game world and engaging in turn-based Pokémon battles. The ad features gameplay accompanied by 8-bit music that is framed within a Nintendo 3DS system. In the final scene, the gameplay is replaced by a screen showing three Nintendo 3DS consoles paired with different Pokémon versions alongside on-screen text stating that the game is available through the Nintendo eShop.

An advertisement for the Chocolate Lolly Maker by John Adams shows children using a pink chocolate making device to melt, pour, and mold chocolate into heart shaped lollipops. The commercial demonstrates kids adding chocolate pieces, filling molds, inserting sticks, and wrapping the finished treats. The commercial concludes by showcasing the kit, accessories, and completed lollies alongside the boxed product, ending with the Chocolate Lolly Maker title screen and the website chocolatelollymaker.com. This ad is targeted towards kids with upbeat music.

This is an advertisement for mystress.it in which two women in an office setting enter a copy room and surprisingly change into their swimsuits to 'sunbathe' under the intense light of a photocopier. They then proceed to pose for multiple scans, while a message in Italian appears, questioning, 'Are you in need of a break?' along with the website's link. The advertisement underscores the high levels of stress experienced in a work environment and presents the promoted travel platform as a remedy for individuals seeking a much-needed getaway.

An advertisment for ThinkPad X3000 shows a person's hands taking a Macbook Air out of an envelope and plugging in accessories with excessive cables, before attempting to fit the Macbook and all of the accessories back in the envelope and failing. The hands then take a ThinkPad X3000 out of an envelope and open it with no cables or extra accessories before closing it, as text graphics appear that say, 'We don't add stuff on. We build it in.' The ad emphasizes that the ThinkPad is designed to work without extra attachment and promotes ThinkPad as a more efficient and simplistic option.

An advertisement for McDonald’s shows a woman eating a chocolate-covered ice-cream while making playful facial expressions and sticking her tongue out to someone off-screen as upbeat and cheerful music plays. The ad promotes the company as friendly and encouraging child-like joy with a fun and lighthearted tone.

An advertisement for Epic Reads promoting the book The Siren cuts between a woman in a dress walking along the shoreline and ocean waves, both overlaid with lines of text from the book as a woman sings. The ad shows the woman looking out at the beach and sky before a man approaches her. She smiles and hugs him, then opens her eyes with a blank expression as they embrace. The singing ends and the ad cuts to water visuals with wave sounds while the author’s name, a #1 New York Times bestselling author of The Selection series, is displayed along with an image of the book and links to download the song. The ad finishes with a page showing other videos and encouraging viewers to subscribe; the tone of the ad is ominous.

An advertisement for Carbuyer.co.uk shows a young man cleaning his car before offering advice. The scene switches to an old lady trimming her hedges before she offers her advice. Lastly the scene switches to an old man sipping coffee in his garage offering advice on which car to buy, before the narrator states that none of the people shown are good options, and rather the viewer should go to Carbuyer.co.uk for trusted reviews, owner opinions, and expert advice. The ad is presented in a comedic tone.

An advertisement for Bernie Sanders’s 2016 presidential campaign shows Sanders speaking directly to the camera while addressing his plan to regulate Wall Street. As animated graphics and text appear on the screen, he narrates his approach centering on breaking up big banks, closing tax loopholes, and requiring corporations to pay higher taxes. The ad highlights these policies as a way to redirect resources towards healthcare and universal college education and concludes with Bernie speaking to the camera again and approving his message.

A McDonald’s advertisement shows Michael Jordan sitting on a basketball court with a McDonald’s bag containing a Big Mac and fries as Larry Bird challenges him to a shootout for his meal. The two legends go back and forth making increasingly difficult trick shots from different spots inside the arena, then take the competition outside as they plan even bigger shots. The McDonald’s jingle plays throughout, including the verse “what you want is what you get,” and Big Mac shots are intercut toward the end. The ad ends with them still competing.

An advertisement for Qantas Airlines opens by showing the in-flight experience, from economy to first class, of travelers of different genders and ages who enjoy the various food and entertainment options. The ad features a shot capturing the exterior of a Qantas aircraft in air, followed by several scenic images of Australia: a boat cruising in the ocean, a young lady surfing, an up-close koala, nighttime views of Sydney, and finally a fireworks display. The ad highlights the variety of activities and landscapes offered by Sydney, and encourages viewers to explore Qantas Airlines' latest deals to Sydney.

This is a PSA campaign for GetUp.org to end marriage discrimination. The video follows a man going about his daily life from the point of view of his partner. It shows a series of life events of meeting the partner, playing on the beach, meeting the parents, parents falling ill and birthdays. The video ends with the man proposing to his partner in front of his family and friends as the camera pans out to reveal it to be a same sex relationship, every time appears elated. The PSA then cuts to the tag line saying 'It's time. End marriage discrimination.' Emphasizing that same sex marriages and relationships look just like heterosexual relationships.

An advertisement for a free informational video about acne shows a man speaking directly to the camera about his experience with skin problems. As he describes what he has tried, the comments people make about him, and his struggles, informational text appears on screen with acne facts that counter what he is saying. The footage finally transitions to him stepping outside with clearer skin and a smile as a voice-over encourages viewers to call for information on fixing acne with contact information.

An advertisement for Dell shows a construction worker singing in the dark as another worker appears and the lights turn on. Four construction workers sing and dance in a barbershop style while standing in a CGI factory filled with colorful mechanical instruments. The machines work together to assemble Dell computers, combining bright pieces as they move through the production line. A stationary machine with five lollipops sticking out is shown while the other machines continue building. The sequence ends with a laptop delivered in a candy wrapper, followed by Dell and Intel branding.

An advertisement for Nescafé shows a woman arriving at a man’s home announcing “It’s coffee time,” as a group of musicians unexpectedly enters and sets up a private concert. Romantic, upbeat music plays while the couple drinks coffee and enjoys the serenade. After the woman leaves, the band continues performing for the man alone. The ad ends with Nescafé branding and text celebrating 100 years of Nestlé. The ad associates the ritual of coffee tasting with pure joy, framing the experience with a sense of celebration and fanfare.

An advertisement for XXX Vitaminwater shows NBA player Steve Nash behind the scenes of the advertisement itself, talking to the camera about how great he is. The ad features Nash having his make up done while talking arrogantly in an over-the-top fashion, comparing himself to the best basketball players and claiming that he is faster than sharks. It highlights the product's suitability for athletic performance by associating it with a professional athlete. The ad is presented in a humorous tone.

An advertisement for Cadbury Dairy Milk shows a young woman with fresh henna dye on her hands struggling to open a chocolate bar. Romantic music plays as she attempts to pick up and open the bar using her elbows and chin in a series of comedic moments. She eventually opens the chocolate while sitting on her bed and is shown smiling and making celebratory gestures before eating it. The ad is presented in a comedic and lighthearted tone.

An advertisement for Dove shows a montage of diverse women going through their daily routines such as boxing, walking a dog, taking photos, and posing for the camera. Voice over plays of the women talking about how their physical appearance has been questioned or criticized, but that they will not change to fit the expectations of others, and text branding appears saying #MyBeautyMySay. The ad emphasizes the importance of embracing everyone's uniqueness and beauty, using an inspirational tone aimed at women.

An advertisement for Copa America Centenario USA 2016 shows a montage of football (soccer) games intercutting with graphics and animations of famous football players as a rhythmic drumbeat plays. Text graphics appear encouraging audiences to see 'the world's best in the U.S.' The ad promotes the football matches as lively and something you don't want to miss, and is presented in an upbeat and epic tone.

An advertisement for National Retail Federation features Dave's Soda and Pet City and its aquatic department manager, Matt, who explains his role in the store and why he likes his job. The ad shows him explaining how he maintains aquariums, cares for animals, assists customer, and manages equipment in the store. Upbeat music plays as he describes how daily problems are handled as part of store operations. The ad highlights what day-to-day work is like in a pet retail environment and is presented in an informative and friendly tone.

A bank advertisement for ICICI Bank shows a panicked man running into a living room telling his friend that he is late to transfer money. His friend tells him to transfer it online and helps him use a computer to complete the transfer. The man looks relieved as company branding appears. The ad promotes ICICI Bank's online transferring service as being quick and easy to use.

An advertisement for 1st for Women Insurance shows a car full of men parked on the side of a mountain road, with one man trying to get back into the vehicle. Every time the man is close to reaching the car, the car drives a little bit forward causing the man to run after the car while the men inside the car laugh, until the car drives over a cliff and crashes. Text graphics appear saying 'why we insure women only', as the first man looks back at the camera. The ad promotes safe driving and care with a humorous tone.

An Acorns advertisement uses colorful animated graphics to show a card being swiped and spare change rounding up from everyday purchases. A voiceover explains that the service automatically invests the extra change to help users build a diversified portfolio over time. The video includes simple charts and growth visuals alongside shots of the Acorns app on a phone and a computer screen. The ad ends with a prompt to download the app with acorns branding.

A PSA for Smarter Fuel Future shows CGI footage of a corn field going from healthy green crops to withered brown crops as a voice over talks about ending ethanol mandates. Text graphics appear over the footage with media quotes and statistics supporting the voice over before the video ends with a logo and wesbite. The ad is presented in a serious and informative tone and associates ethanol mandates with low crop yields, encouraging viewers to speak to congress to fix this.

An advertisement for Perfect Brownie shows its brownie pan in different usage scenarios with an informative voice over. It opens with black and white footage of a man frustrated by a low quality pan from another brand where the brownie sticks. The ad then transitions to colorful footage with a friendly and uplifting tone to demonstrate this product's non-stick quality during baking, slicing, and serving. It includes joyful scenes of family parties, kids having fun, and adults smiling to illustrate their satisfaction with the product and its versatility in making various desserts. Finally, it emphasizes the price and the bonus accessories the product comes with for $19.95.

An advertisement for Audi shows a black Audi R8 driving through a parking lot with a security guard watching. The car stops and a woman gets out, the same time as a man with a gun walks over and the security guard appears and tells him to drop the gun. The man threatens to shoot the car instead of the woman, and the security guard gives up and puts his gun down as the man escapes. Text and branding appears a glamour shots of the car are shown. The ad promotes the Audi R8 as a car with prestige status using a mysterious, cinematic tone.

An advertisement for Jacobs Krönung coffee shows a man sleepwalking out of his bedroom window and wandering through the city. He carefully steps across ledges and obstacles, narrowly avoiding accidents, as surprised bystanders react and watch him pass. The man eventually reaches ground level and sits down to drink a cup of coffee, finally waking up and realizing he is in a random family’s backyard. Set to Ray Charles’ “I Love Her So,” the ad uses a warm, humorous tone to suggest Jacobs Krönung brings people together.

The advertisment for Just Eat opens with four friends relaxing in an apartment when one of them shows his phone displaying the Just Eat logo, prompting him to start singing as the others join in singing and dancing while the music builds into a catchy song centered around the Just Eat brand. Finally, the music briefly cuts out before returning as one one of the friends open the door to a delivery driver who is holding food from Just eat and says, “OMG, I’m back again,” bringing the vocals back in for a playful finish.

A Toyota documentary advertisement opens with a woman holding a photo of her destroyed home, then on screen text reads “10 years after Katrina.” Footage of flooded neighborhoods and storm damage is intercut with residents rebuilding and repairing homes as a man speaks about wanting to do good work about needing some direction. Toyota branding appears as the ad emphasizes Toyota's desire to be apart of the community to rebuild St. Benard.

This advertisement for Ontario as a travel destination opens with a montage of a variety of landscapes, settings, and activities, including mountains, churches, lakes, cliff jumping, surfing, archery, skating, and cultural experiences. The ad highlights Ontario's natural beauty, ranging from forests to snow covered mountains, while emphasizing the diversity of activities to participate in and the cultural diversity of Ontario. The narrator personifies the region by speaking in first person and prompts the audience to guess the location by repeatedly asking, 'Where Am I?' The answer is revealed when Ontario is displayed in big, bold letters on the screen at the conclusion of the montage.

An advertisment for Seven Knights shows a fantasy video game world and monsters walking toward camera with a mountain behind them. A montage shows anime-style human characters posing and fighting the monsters with swords and magical powers. The human characters look up as dragon lands and roars at them and they jump into battle. The ad ends promoting the mobile game Seven Knights with their branding and pushing the viewer to download the game with the text 'Download Seven Knights Today!'

An advertisement shows a giraffe walking across a savanna while a gazelle runs nearby. Two lions watch the gazelle as it continues running and then collides with a tree, prompting one of the lions to look at the other. Rhythmic background music plays throughout the scene. The ad is presented in a humorous tone.

A UNICEF promo shows a young boy speaking in a foreign language in a worn, sparsely furnished room while English subtitles translate his words about his situation and concern for his younger brother. The video cuts between close-ups of the boy and wider shots where his younger brother is visible resting on bedding in the background. Toward the end, the subtitles shift to an on-screen message stating that likes do not save lives and that money does, followed by the UNICEF logos promoting to donate to the organization to help the cause.

A PSA for the Malala Fund shows fast edited photos of Malala Yousafzai giving speeches, as well as close up photos of girls wearing veils. Malala is shown speaking to camera and text appears saying her goal is to give women 'a voice so loud, the world will listen.' A fast montage of photos of girls in school is shown, and ends with Malala walking in slow motion with some girls.

An advertisement for Motorola shows a man standing on the street dropping his cell phone while talking to the camera about how often people break their phones. Animated graphics of the phone's interior structure are shown and then a montage plays of the man dropping his phone in various locations around New York City. Later, the man shows that the phone got a few dents, but the screen didn't shatter. The ad promotes a durable phone screen for people who often damage their phones, using a comedic and informational tone.

An advertisement for Bridgestone shows an employee in an office talking to a colleague who tells him he accidentally hit Reply All in an email. In a frantic attempt to stop the recipients from seeing the response, quick montages show the man driving around the city stealing and smashing other people's laptops, computers, and cell phones. He returns to the office where the other man tells him he was wrong and that the email was only sent to him. The ad promotes Bridgestone as a strong and reliable tire company.

An advertisement for Big Babol bubble gum opens with three children and their dog sitting on a park bench, with one child holding an open package of the product.  A mini animated jelly character jumps out of the bag and briefly bounces on and off their heads and around the park while the children try to catch it. This is followed by the children and the dog putting the bubble gum in their mouths and blowing large bubbles. This ad promotes Big Babol with a humorous tone, targeting children.

A PSA against drug use shows a substance boiling in a pan accompanied by dramatic music. An egg is dropped into the pan and a voice over says, 'this is your brain on drugs.' This ad uses the egg to metaphorically suggest that drugs cause the brain fry, and is presented in a serious and informative tone.

An advertisement for Kinder Joy shows a bored brother and sister at home asking their mother to buy them something surprising, fun, and sweet while she goes shopping. At the store, she selects Kinder Joy and returns home, where the children excitedly open the packaging to reveal a toy and chocolate treats. The commercial highlights the toy surprise, crispy wafer balls with milk and chocolate, and the children enjoying them with a small spoon and at the end giving their mom 3 kisses. It ends with a product shot, toy lineup, and the on screen text 'The 3-in-1 joy'.

An advertisement for the video game 2014 FIFA World Cup Brazil shows football player Landon Donavan in a hotel room, getting out of bed, making and drinking coffee, knocking over a gold trophy, and playing a football video game on a PlayStation. He scores a goal in the video game and looks at the camera with a smirk as the text 'always in the game' appears, followed by a final scene of Landon singing about not going to Brazil and laughing, while showing product packaging and EA Sports branding. The ad promotes the videogame as relaxing and fun, using a humorous and self-aware tone.

This advertisement is a short commercial skit featuring K-pop performers at the 2015 Mnet Asian Music Awards in Hong Kong. The main character, V, is shown holding a small, folded origami card while standing in a hallway, followed by brief interactions with other K-pop members in a restroom area. V mistakenly tries to give the card to numerous K-pop performers, where he then has to apologize for disrupting them. Finally, V finds the right person and runs away, who then opens the card to see it’s a message about the 30-day countdown to the 2015 Mnet Asian Music Awards.

This Allstate insurance advertisement reflects on the company's founding during the Great Depression, highlighting its resilience through numerous economic recessions. The narrator explains that after times of hardship, people often return to 'the basics,' such as family meals and simple outdoor activities. By showcasing nostalgic imagery of everyday life, the ad positions Allstate as a reliable protector of these fundamental values, concluding with a twist on their well-known slogan, 'Put them in good hands.'

A PSA about Proposition 8 shows a young girl running into a kitchen and telling her mother that she learned at school she can marry a girl. A male professor in a suit then appears superimposed over the footage; he states that the court ruled parents have no legal right to object and quotes the California Constitution.  The ad ends with on-screen messaging that emphasizes the need for parents and society to intervene in marriage education for children.

A reflective PSA campaign for Everytown.org for gun safety. The video starts with a  boy and a girl playing hide and seek in a house. As the boy counts, the girl runs upstairs to hide. She then finds an unsecured gun in a box and, while playing with it, accidentally discharges the gun when the boy runs into the room to find her. The video then cuts to a PSA warning saying scenes like this happens all the time and to start the conversation about responsible gun ownership in your home and community.

An advertisement for Sprint shows Peyton Manning wearing a fake mustache disguise while showing a flip phone in a garage. The flip phone screen shows a football game and he says that you can watch football highlights of any game including Peyton Manning's, if you are a fan of him. The ad wraps up with a voice over that gives information about the cell phone offer as text information and branding for Sprint appears.

An advertisment for McDonalds shows a woman and a boy arriving at a McDonalds counter and greeting another woman and girl. The girl shows the boy that she dips her fries in her chocolate sundae, causing his eyes to widen, and she then takes him by the hand as they run around the resturant. The scene transitions into the same boy and girl as adults, with the woman draging him to meet her husband and daughter, which makes him frown. The man and woman, and her family, sit at a table and eat McDonalds and the man now dips his fries in his chocolate sundae which makes the woman smile.

An advertisement for the Fujifilm Instax Mini 90 portable instant camera, showing various angles of same model cameras popping their instant film photographs out of the camera which are cute baby pictures. The ad features pop and upbeat music while many different baby's photographs are put into scrapbooks. It highlights sharing original photos with the hashtag #myinstaxstory and slogan 'Share an original!'

An advertisement for McDonalds shows a birds eye view of a stadium, a baksetball court, and fans cheering, as a voice over says 'when you're you're the next big thing, everybody wants you...even Kobe Bryant.' Which then cuts to Kobe Bryant eating a burger in a locker room, before transitioning to close up shots of a McDonalds burger. Kobe finishes his burger and throws the wrapper in the trash can which misses, causing him to have a confused expression. The ad ends with McDonalds logo and their slogan 'we love to see you smile' promoting their brand.

An advertisement for SunDrop citrus soda features a woman performing dance moves in various locations after drinking the soda. The ad features Snoop Dogg's 'Drop It Like It's Hot' playing in the background as the woman dances enthusiastically on the street, on the beach, and in a canoe while holding the drink. By the end, a group of young adults dance around the woman at the pool, holding the soda with smiles on their faces. This ad is presented in a humorous tone.

The advertisement follows Peyton Lambton from HGTV’s Growing Yard as she redecorates the landing area of her home. She transforms one side of the space into a man cave for her husband, featuring a sectional sofa, an entertainment center with a TV stand, an orange chair, and a blue patterned rug. The ad then shifts to the adjacent area—Peyton’s workstation—which includes a large desk, a gallery wall with a “good vibes only” framed print, and a bookshelf. The ad highlights different ways to redecorate and concludes with a promotional screen featuring a “Click Here” button directing viewers to Wayfair.com.

This Carl's JR video advertises the Memphis BBQ burger. Two girls are shown fighting for dominance over a grill; one girl cooking burgers, and the other cooking pulled pork. They ultimately realize the foods can be combined, and both take a bite of their burgers, arms interlinked. The advertisement adopts an alluring, yet humorous approach, and highlights how mouthwatering Carl's JR is.

The advertisement for the game Summoners War showcases an intense fantasy battles among imaginative characters, including winged warriors, elemental beings, and powerful dragons. The promo features rock music and fast-paced combat across dramatic environments such as volcanic landscapes and ancient ruins, emphasizing the game's strategic summoning mechanics and team-based fights. Toward the end, there is an on-screen message, 'The one true Summoner will save the world', inviting players to enter the Sky Arena. The video closes with Summoners War branding with the text 'The Sky Arena awaits' followed by the Com2us logo.

An advertisement for Parrot Bebop 2 drones opens with a man launching a drone from an observatory and piloting it across sweeping outdoor landscapes. The footage alternates between the drone flying through open skies and the drone’s camera view capturing rolling fields, beaches, mountains, and landmarks. Epic, cinematic music plays as the drone glides smoothly through each location, ending with it flying toward the sunset as the branding appears. The ad emphasizes the drone’s stability, range, and performance in a variety of environments.

An advertisement for T.D.M. Auto Sales features a man speaking directly to the camera, introducing himself as a former gynecologist from Cuba who now sells cars in the United States. The commercial alternates between him delivering pun-based marketing lines and scenes at a used car lot, where he gestures toward vehicles and dances while two musicians play a guitar and a trumpet behind him. The ad ends by displaying the TDM Auto Sales location at 1631 S. Main St., High Point, NC; their phone number, 336-882-2277; and their website, www.TDMautosales.com.

An Ikea advertisement opens in a Renaissance era European home where a family is ready to eat, but the father of the household brings in a painter to create a still life of the meal first. Intense violin music plays as the family waits, time passes on a clock, and two men then carry the painting around town seeking approval at each stop. Including a couple in bed,  a pistol duel, and a fancy dinner party. It cuts to modern day with the same family as the father obsesses over a food photo. The tagline appears 'Its a meal not a competition, lets relax' After seeing his daughter waiting, he puts the phone down and eats with his family. Emphasizing that the time spent together as a family is what is actually important not the validation of others.

This advertisement for BuzzFeed shows a man entering a subway station and ordering two sandwiches from Subway. He then returns home as a voiceover explains, over step-by-step clips, how to turn the two sandwiches into stuffing. After the stuffing is described as the perfect last-minute Thanksgiving meal, the ad cuts to Michael Phelps sitting down to enjoy his Subway order as the “$5 Footlong” jingle plays, claiming that the stuffing is perfect for someone who is friends with Michael Phelps. The target audience includes Michael Phelps fans and viewers looking for a convenient Thanksgiving stuffing dish.

This advertisement showcases The Animal, a powerful 4x4 toy truck by Galoob designed to overcome rugged terrain. The ad demonstrates the truck’s unique 'claws' that emerge from its tires to provide extra traction for climbing over rocks and through water. With a high-energy jungle theme, the commercial highlights the vehicle's durability and off-road capabilities, targeting children who enjoy action-oriented play.

This is an advertisement for Google Chrome web browser. The video follows Daniel and Jennifer Northcutt and their journey in opening a restaurant. The videos show the couple talking about their experiences as different functions on Google Chrome from Google Maps, to websites and Google reviews help them make their business run. The video ends with the tag line saying 'the web is what you make of it' indicating that Google Chrome can be anything one makes of it and can do all sorts of functions to help a business flourish.

A Volkswagen advertisement focuses on how sturdy and well-built the car is, emphasizing its solid construction and tight assembly. The car is shown being lifted on a hoist and dropped as a durability test, reinforcing how well it holds together. The narration also mentions thorough paint coverage on both the exterior and hidden interior areas to help protect against corrosion. A humorous comment about the car being airtight is made just before it goes into the water. The video ends with the Volkswagen logo on screen.

An advertisement for Castro Dresses opens in a hotel lobby where a blonde woman in a strapless red dress draws attention from several men and plays into the spotlight. A female hotel server flirts with her and leads her to a private room. As a fashion-themed song plays, the server blindfolds the woman and kisses her, creating a seductive distraction. The woman appears to expect a romantic encounter, and in the moment, the server discreetly takes the red dress and leaves. The ad ends with Castro Dresses branding and the line, “Take it when you have the chance,” in a provocative tone. Emphasizing when you see the dress you must have it for yourself.

An advertisement for the Lumix GX80 camera from Panasonic shows a boy walking to a diving board at a hotel pool as his mom prepares to take a photo. The boy dives and poses in mid air and the mom takes a video-picture which she is able to rewind and choose a frame from, which is shown being saved and transitioning into a frame on a wall. A voice over explains the process over graphics, before cutting back to the pool where a man and girl show award-signs that say 10. The ad promotes the camera's ease of use in capturing moments in an informational and lighthearted tone.

This Tumbl Trak advertisement shows two young girls practicing gymnastics at home. Throughout the video, either the mother speaks directly to the camera or one of the daughters speaks while the mother and the other daughter appear alongside her. The mother explains how she discovered Tumbl Trak while searching for a safe way for her daughters to practice at home, since they were constantly building their own equipment. The speaking daughter explains that she likes the toy because it allows them to play and practice at home, while time at the gym is primarily focused on skill-based training. The advertisement emphasizes how Tumbl Trak helps the girls safely develop their skills and prepare for training in a real gym environment, targeting young gymnasts and their parents.

An advertisement for Kmart shows a customer in a department store talking to a storeperson who tells him he can 'ship his pants.' The man then tells his family who react excitedly, before cutting to other customers saying they also 'ship their pants' among other things. The family is shown hugging the storeperson as Kmart branding appears. The ad is presented in a self-aware and humourous tone.

An advertisement for the mobile marketplace platform called 5miles shows a husband and wife sitting on a couch in his man cave when the wife tells him her mother is coming to live with them. The ad features clips of the wife taking photos of the husband's possessions, such as a football jersey and a pinball machine, and selling them through the 5miles mobile app. The wife also purchases a dresser with a mirror through the app and converts the man cave into a bedroom for her mother. The ad highlights the ease of buying and selling items through 5miles and is presented in a humorous tone. In the closing scene, the husband is shown using the app to take photos of the wife's closet in an act of revenge.

An advertisement for Indian Airlines shows a man sitting next to a little girl on an airplane as she teaches him how to use the seatbelt, the reclining chair, and the tray table - getting more and more annoyed each time he doesn't understand. Later on, a stewardess approaches the man holding a pilot's uniform and tells him that the next flight that he is piloting will be on time, and he asks for a blanket for the girl who is now sleeping. The ad emphasizes that Indian Airlines employees are just like their passengers and are invested in everyone's well being as they are caring and friendly.

The upbeat Pepsi commercial uses a music-and-dance theme to celebrate Michael Jackson’s influence and connect it to youth culture. Set to the beat of “Billie Jean” with Pepsi-inspired lyrics, kids of different ages dress in MJ’s signature look and dance in the street, hitting his iconic moves in unison. Michael steps into the scene and reinforces the message of a whole new generation. Alfonso takes the lead at the end, and the spot freeze-frames on: “Pepsi, The Choice of a New Generation.”

An advertisement for a Poonikins t-shirt shows a man wearing a horse head running on a treadmill to upbeat dance music as a woman walks in and looks unimpressed. The music continues as a montage shows the horse-man lifting weights, getting chased by a dog through a parking lot, standing on the beach, reading a book, and dancing. The montage ends with the horse-man dancing infront of the woman, who can't hear the music that the horse-man is dancing to and walks away. Product branding appears and a final scene is shown of the horse-man reading and a woman laughing behind the camera, causing the horse-man to laugh. The ad promotoes the shirt’s versatility in a humorous tone.

An advertisement for the Chrysler Group car brands—Ram, Dodge, Jeep, and Chrysler—is narrated by actor Clint Eastwood. Sombre music plays as slow paced footage of every day Americans, from office workers, to builders, to firemen is shown intercut with images of Detroit car manufacturing plants, ending with Clint Eastwood talking directly to camera. Eastwood reflects on the economic challenges facing the country and parallels them with the economic hardships the city of Detroit has faced, highlighting that just as Detroit, nicknamed Motor City, was able to rebuild, so can the whole nation. The ad is presented in a melancholy and uplifting tone.

A claymation style ad for Brisk Iced Tea  features rapper Eminem. The spot opens with Eminem walking out of a building after rejecting a deal, while an executive is shoved into a car trunk and bills fall to the ground. Eminem then moves through different film sets and a music studio, insisting he refuses to do commercials because he is never allowed to make them his way. After taking a sip of Brisk, he agrees to do the ad, but says he has one final demand. On a rooftop, the executive starts to refuse, saying they cannot change the name to “Eminem Shut Up and Drink It,” but Eminem knocks him off the ledge before he can finish. The commercial ends with a colorful lineup of Brisk drinks.

An upbeat advertisement for a perfume brand called Enjoli promotes a fragrance for the working woman. The ad features three women on a set who appear one by one, singing a song about balancing different parts of their lives. One comes out in a robe with a pan in hand, another in a business suit and the last in an evening dress. It highlights how this perfume fits a woman's work, home, and social life.

An advertisement for Twinkle Beauty Parlor shows an Indian man and woman on their wedding night - with him trying to reveal her face under a hood as she tries to avoid him. The man finally removes her hood and reveals that she has a moustache, which causes him to faint. The ad promotes Twinkle Beauty Parlor as the solution fixing her moustache and is presented in a humorous tone.

An advertisement for QuestBar shows a stop motion style instructional video of hands combining the Questbar Cookies & Cream protein bar and Arctic Zero frozen desserts into a meal. The protein bar is shown getting crushed and combined with ice cream before being coated in melted chocolate chips and put in a freezer before being put on a plate. The ad highlights the ease and simplicity of making frozen snacks with the product and is presented in an instructional style.

This is an advertisement for Seagram's Imperial Blue Superhits Music CD. The video open with a man running into an elevator and ignoring two people behind him. He takes it up to the 18th floor only to see a beautiful woman enter. He stays in the elevator and takes it back down to the first floor, but is too shy to talk to the beautiful woman. As they reach the first floor the beautiful woman exits the elevator, and the annoyed people he left behind stare at him as they get on the elevator. The logo of the Seagram's Imperial Blue Superhits Music CD fades in as the tag line 'Men will be men' was read by the narrator, indicating men will like what they like regardless of circumstances.

This informative advertisement for Downy opens with a woman in a lab coat holding a GoPro camera and placing it inside a washing machine. Then it shows footages of clothes spinning vigorously inside the washing machine from different angles, with the text 'The laundry process can damage your clothes.' The ad compares the same cloth with and without using the product, showing the one without using this fabric conditioner is heavily wrinkled. By the end, it displays the product image alongside upbeat music, with the text suggesting that Downy protects clothes from stretching, fading, and fuzz.

An advertisement for Carr Nissan shows a man driving a Nissan in a parody of an action movie trailer with voice over and intense music. A montage is shown of the man firstly at the car dealership, then driving through hilly roads, and then poorly performing extreme stunts like mountain climbing and skydiving. The fantasy ends with the man standing at the dealership only imagining the scenario, before a woman asks if she can also be a part of his fantasy. The ad promotes the idea that owning a Nissan makes you more daring and heroic, and is presented in a humorous tone.

This Gatorade advertisement features NFL quarterback Peyton Manning giving a humorous instructional tutorial to a child on the mechanics of throwing a football. Manning breaks down his technique into three, simplified steps: 'wipe the windshield,' 'elbow your brother,' and 'flick the booger off your finger'. The ad demonstrates these steps using both an overhead diagram and footage of Manning practicing on a field with a young player who catches his throw, “touchdown”. It concludes with Manning in an office saying the brand's tagline, 'Is it in you?', positioning Gatorade as the official sports drink of both Peyton Manning and the NFL.

A product advertisement for home electronics features a family waking up early to surprise the mother of the home. The family interacts with featured Bajaj electronics which also have uniformed assistants helping the family prepare for the surprise. The mother wakes up to prepared breakfast and the family greeting her showing appreciation. The ad ends showcasing the Bajaj electronics while The narrator says 'we are family' emphasizing how Bajaj’s electronics can support all of a family electronic needs.

An advertisement for Dettol soap follows a mother and child as she walks him to the school bus stop. The ad features the mother protecting the child from the dirt and animated germs that appear along their path, but she is unable to protect her child from germs when another child sneezes on him on the school bus. The ad then cuts to a display of Dettol soap, followed by a clip where the child washes himself with soap as the ad highlights the 100% better protection provided by Dettol over other soaps.

An advertisement for Dos Equis shows a bearded man depicted as exceptionally strong, confident, and adventurous across different moments in his life. The ad opens in black and white with scenes of him bench pressing two nurses seated on chairs and arm wrestling a powerful opponent, followed by color footage of him older as he releases a bear caught in a trap. Later appearing in a nightclub, he raises a beer and says, 'I don't drink often, but when I do, it's Dos Equis.' Emphasizing the Dos Equis brand with strong, charismatic, and mature men.

An advertisement for the Separation Anxiety series shows the host questioning a female contestant in front of a live audience, asking her things she should know about her husband. She reacts dramatically when she cannot answer correctly, putting her head in her hands and screaming. A quick montage cuts between the game board, the husband watching and speaking, and the contestant on stage as the host continues the challenge. The ad ends with branding for the show and a company logo.

A Nissan advertisement opens with a helmeted motorcyclist looking over the desert landscape, setting a high-speed racing mood.  It then cuts to a wide to a Nissan sports car speeding down an open road as the driver's voiceover begins and the competition builds.  The motorcyclist joins the road at the same distance, riding alongside the car as fast-cut action shots show the Nissan pushing its speed against the motorcycle, an F1-style car, and a plane. The sequence peaks as the car launches over a hill before promotion for Nissan branding appears with their slogan 'Built for the Human Race'.

An advertisement for King crisps features Connor McGregor and a man seated side by side in suits, introducing the product. The man narrates the brand's story and product ingredients while McGregor eats the crisps, with a crunch sound repeatedly interrupting and censoring the narrator's swear words. McGregor then holds the bag and promotes the product to the viewer, saying a curse word himself while having the sound blocked by the same crisp sound. The ad emphasizes the product's crispiness and good taste in a humorous tone.

An advertisement for Dove Men+Care shows a series of everyday moments highlighting men showing care, effort, and support. Uplifting music plays as the video features men cycling together at sunrise, helping push a stalled vehicle, embracing a child at home, helping a teammate who has fallen and sharing other intimate moments with loved ones. Finally, it cuts to a narrator who says, 'Care makes a man stronger' and the product line is displayed.

An advertisement for Puppy Apartment shows a puppy apartment cage that is sectioned to have a designated potty and sleeping area. Upbeat music plays and text commentates as the camera follows a little black dog exploring the cage, using different entrances and exits, and using the bathroom. The ad ends with a site where viewers can learn more about this 'one-of-a-kind' system.

An advertisement for Fiat/SEAT shows a red sports car driving up to a white Fiat at a stop light. The driver of the red sports car revs his engine to try and start a race and when the traffic light goes green the red sports car drives away but the white Fiat doesn't move. The driver of the white Fiat has a pleased expression as a woman lifts her head from his lap implying a sexually suggestive act has happened. The ad promotes the idea that the car makes you attractive and is presented in a humorous and suggestive tone.

An parody political advertisement for Herman Cain shows a flag and a man pulling his hair while a voice over says South Carolina doesn't have a candidate. A montage shows images of debates, dancers, and American flags intercut with an image of comedian and talk-show host Stephen Colbert as Herman Cain. Sketches of Stephen Colbert dressed in funny outfits continue to play, ending with an uninterupted shot of Colbert giving a creepy smile. The ad uses satirical humor and comedy.

A campaign advertisement for Bernie Sanders for President shows a montage of people working, spending time with family, and attending Bernie Sander's rallies. Text graphics are shown saying 'they've all come to look for America,' as a song sings the same lyrics, and people are shown cheering at rallies intercut with footage of Bernie Sanders talking to them and speaking on stage. The ad promotes unity with a hopeful tone.

An advertisement for Vittoria coffee shows a black and white montage of Al Pacino walking around New York City. A close up of a coffee cup is shown intercut with footage of people cleaning the street, buying bread, and running. A voice over from Al Pacino explains that he needs coffee to feel good at work. The ad ends with him talking to a person off camera, with a coffee cup in front of him that shows the Vittoria branding in gold color while the rest of the video remains in black and white, with Al promoting the Vittoria coffee saying 'This is good coffee.'

An advertisement for CollegeHumor begins with text explaining that Photoshop promotes unrealistic beauty standards for men and women, including celebrities. The ad cuts to a live Photoshop session where an editor removes the digital enhancements applied to his body before transforming him into a human-shaped feces and then just feces. The ad ends with the message to be proud of who you are even if you are a piece of shit,' followed by Mike Trapp asking viewers to subscribe to the CollegeHumor channel. The tone of the advertisement is humorous.

An advertisement for the Nokia Lumia 920 cell phone shows guests at a wedding filming the ceremony on their cell phones before angrily disagreeing on which phone is better. A bombastic song plays as the wedding guests get into an over-exagerated physical fight and two staff members film them with Nokia Lumia 920 phones. The staff members ask each other if the guests would still be fighting if they knew about the Nokia Lumia 920, and text and graphics appears that says, 'Don't fight. Switch.' The ad presents the Nokia as unique amongst other phones and is shown in a whimsical and humorous tone.

A man sits at an outdoor Burger King table with a woman, girl, and boy while he play fights with a vintage Hulk toy and modern day Hulk toy. He makes the vintage Hulk defeat the modern one and mocks it in a high pitched voice. Suddenly, a life-size Hulk  jumps from a nearby buliding and smashes their table, causing them to scream. The scene cuts to a narrator introducing the 6 collectable toys and how to obtain them. The advertisement ends with the lifesize hulk pushing aside a Burger king resturant to reveal burger king's slogan 'Have it your way' before cutting back to the man screaming at the Hulk.

An advertisement for Sprint shows two men comparing the capabilities of their phones in a locker room. One man claims his phone has crime deterrent and proves it by challenging the other man to take his wallet, and when the other man obliges, he chucks the phone at him and knocks him down to the ground. The ad associates its product with humor, while highlighting that their phones now have live TV, wireless music downloads, email, and crime deterrent.

An advertisement for Diesel shows two cars - one decorated as a butt, and one decorated as a shoe - chasing each other across desert landscapes. The butt-car crashes into a rock and the shoe-car drives into it, which fades to both cars stuck together driving into the sunset. Text and branding appears with a quote that says 'great for kicking asses.' The ad presents the idea that Diesel makes 'kick ass' shoes and is shown in a cinematic and humorous tone.

A Zippo advertisement shows a man getting gasoline poured on him by two men in coats. The men in coats light a matchbook, but its blown out by the wind. The man in gasoline laughs while rolling on the ground which causes a Zippo lighter to fall out of his pocket. The men in coats light up the Zippo lighter instead and turn to the camera and smile as branding appears. The ad promotes the reliability of Zippo through parody of Blaxploitation films.

An lighthearted and friendly advertisement for New York Bakery Texas Toast opens with an older man holding a wooden board with with five slices of bread. He is identified as, Don Penn, the inventor of this product. The ad cuts between Don with his grandchildren and bakers holding loaves and waving as a cheerful group, which emphasizing tradition and family. Two bakers then hold up garlic and cheese, with the narration saying 'Topped with real garlic and cheese,' followed by product images.

An advertisement for Burger King opens with the Burger King mascot dancing with girls in SpongeBob-themed costumes on a SpongeBob-themed set as a SpongeBob-style rendition of Baby Got Back plays. Clips of SpongeBob characters dancing on a television are intercut throughout the scene. After the dancing segment ends, the mascot presents a SpongeBob-themed Burger King meal bag priced at 99 cents. The scene then pulls back into a living room where two girls and a man are watching, and the man comments, “Booty is booty.” The advertisement ends with an animated 99-cent emblem and realistic versions of SpongeBob characters displayed on the SpongeBob island alongside the meal package, as a narrator announces the price and that the meal includes a toy.

An advertisement for Evian bottled water shows an adult man walking down a city street and seeing his reflection through a mirror as a dancing child. As other pedestrians pass by, they also notice their reflection appear as a playful children, and the group begins dancing together in synchronized, energetic movements. The commercial presents this upbeat visual effect to suggest youthfulness and vitality. It ends by showing Evian bottles with the on screen message 'Drink pure and natural.'

An PSA for Aaj Tak shows a busy marketplace where an old man is asking a young man to stop smoking a cigarette in front of him. The old man force feeds the young man chilli vegetables and when he protests, the old man tells him that he is doing the equivalent of what the young man was doing to him. The young man leaves and a third man tells the old man he did the right thing as Aaj Tak branding appears. The PSA promotes anti-smoking in a humorous tone.

An advertisement for vote4energy.org shows a woman standing against a white background talking about why she supports oil and natural gas. She explains that pro-energy policies provide millions more jobs in different industries with good paychecks that would benefit future generations. Text appears showing data from an independent study and promotes the political campaign in an informative tone.

An advertisement for Nescafe Classic instant coffee shows a group of attractive young adults relaxing on a tropical beach with an island party vibe and reggae-style music. The focus shifts to a man with dreadlocks mixing instant coffee into a bottle of water before pouring it into a glass with ice. A woman in a bikini walks over to him holding her glass, and they exchange flirty eye contact as he fills her drink. He then looks up to see a group of women waiting with glasses, and the scene turns into a lively beach gathering with everyone enjoying the coffee.

A Nike advertisement shows a man in a Nike shirt and sneakers running down a dirt road. He slows to walk and appears to argue with himself about giving up. The ad cuts between angles of him as the internal debate continues. Then he starts running again with on-screen text saying, 'leave your old self behind.' The tone is motivational and emphasizes perseverance and mental toughness.

An advertisement for Sword of Chaos shows 3D animated fantasy characters in stylized battle outfits. A female warrior looks up at the camera, draws her sword, and charges toward another armed woman with a gun. The two clash in combat before a third woman appears using magical powers. The action builds into a fast-paced battle sequence with dramatic effects as the game’s branding 'Sword of Chaos' appears on screen.

An advertisement for the Sony Bravia New LCD Television opens with a montage of apartment buildings, houses, and hilly sidewalks. The ad features colorful balls which gradually increase in number bouncing down the sidewalk, rolling down a hill, flooding the street and filling the screen, pouring out of a downspout as a frog jumps out, and eventually falling from the sky. The vibrant and colorful balls in the ad highlight the television's advanced color technology.

This advertisement for M&T Bank features customers Andrea and Harold Harden sharing how their children inspire them through life's transitions. The couple discusses the fulfillment of guiding and protecting their family, while the bank emphasizes that understanding these personal values is central to their service. The ad concludes with a shot of the M&T Bank flag and a call to action to learn more about the Hardens' story on the bank’s website.

An advertisement for Boss Coffee opens in a Japanese restaurant where people are enjoying a late-night meal. The ad focuses on two men finishing their food while having a conversation. As they leave, the camera shifts to Tommy Lee Jones sitting next to them and eating. The camera then follows Tommy Lee Jones outside as he looks toward the brightening sky, where Japanese text appears as a narrator speaks, while he drinks from a rainbow-colored Boss Coffee can. The advertisement concludes with a black screen displaying the Boss Coffee can and brand name.

An advertisement for Bud Light features a segment from the “Real Men of Genius” series. The ad features a man ordering a giant taco salad as the narrator comments on the high-calorie ingredients, and this is stitched with clips of a vocalist and backup singers delivering praise for the giant taco salad in a studio performance. The man is shown enjoying the giant taco salad in a cafeteria and on an exercise bicycle, finally clipping to a scene of a Bud Light being grabbed from the cooler as the narrator encourages pairing the salad with the beer. The ad is presented in a humorous tone.

An advertisement for South Korean fried chicken shows two children at home watching RoboCop on television while their mother cooks. RoboCop suddenly emerges from the TV, approaches the mother, eats a piece of fried chicken, and nods in approval. The family reacts with shock as RoboCop then picks up their refrigerator. The advertisement ends with a simple product shot of the fried chicken brand and is presented in a comedic tone.

An advertisement for Friskies hosts a game show called 'Will Kitty Play With It,' beginning with an excited narrator and animated gameshow introduction announcing the show's name and introducing Digger, a cat, her profile, and the item up for play's profile, a spork. It then pans to Digger on a couch in a living space as the narrator comments while the camera follows her attention being caught by a cardboard box with a question mark. The box is lifted to reveal the spork, which Digger examines and begins to play with, making it a success with slow-motion clips highlighting the moment after. The ad ends with an animated gameshow outro showing the show's name, other play items, the friskies logo, and the Twitter hashtag 'WillKittyPlay'. The ad is humorous.

A political advertisement accuses the Human Society of the United States and its CEO Wayne Pacelle of corruption. The ad opens with a graphic showing Bernie Madoff morphing into Wayne Pacelle, followed by animated images of dogs arranged in a grid to suggest that less than in one percent of donations go to animal shelters. Then it shows Pacelle speaking at the podium alongside visuals of court buildings, lawyers and newspaper headlines referencing lawsuits and racketeering allegations. The add suggests the viewers should stop donating to the organization and instead give directly to local animal shelters.

An advertisement for Sprite shows a boy in a suburban home answering the door to find a wrestler named The Sting asking if he's 'ready to wrestle?' The boy brings The Sting inside, his parents clear the room, and the boy drinks a can of sprite before the Sting starts to punch him and throw him around the house in a wrestling match as his parents film it on a camcorder. The parents say 'it looks so real', before Sprite branding appears promoting their product.

In an advertisement promoting Microsoft Windows 95, a sequence of scenes are shown to demonstrate the software’s adaptability in various environments, such as educational institutions, workplaces, and bustling urban areas. The ad wraps up by portraying the operating system as a versatile answer for advancing both personal and career endeavors. Set to the energetic tune of the Rolling Stones' classic “Start Me Up,” the commercial emphasizes the significance of the fresh “Start” feature for managing activities like editing documents, playing games, and engaging online.

An advertisement for Meox Mix promotes its cat food varieties. The ad features a tabby cat against a black background singing in cat speak with captions below describing the product details. It then cuts two a product shot showing the two flavors, Original and Seafood followed by footage of the food being poured in a bowl and a final shot of cat Meowing. The ad highlights how much cats love the medley of seafood, chicken, turkey and ocean-fish flavors and is presented in a playful tone.

An advertisement for the HTC One A9 mobile phone shows a man performing parkour through a series of environments. The ad features dramatic music overlayed with scenes of the man climbing a building behind a group of uniformed individuals marching in military formation, the man running across a warehouse where workers repeatedly stamp papers, and the man crashing down from the ceiling into a dining room where seated mannequins appear. As he moves through these spaces, on-screen text highlights phone features such as a Super Thin All-Metal Design, 24-Bit High-Res Audio, and a 13MP Camera. Additional text reading “Be bold,” “Be different,” “Be loud,” and “Be inspired” appears over the footage as the man continues his parkour. The ad is presented in a dramatic tone.

An advertisement shows a dark blue Ford Sportka parked in a driveway. A cat walks onto the driveway where the sunroof opens and the cat approaches the car. The cat jumps onto the car and sticks its head into the sunroof that begins to close on its head, resulting in decapatation. The caption 'FordSportka, The Ka's evil twin displays on screen above the car and finally cuts to a black screen that displays the site www.the-eviltwin.co.uk.

An advertisement for Papa John's shows a man handmaking a pizza from scratch by stretching dough, adding sauce and toppings, and preparing it to bake, while a narrator explains the company's quality guarantee: 'Love your pizza or get another one free.' The ad highlights that customers can get any large pizza with up to 5-toppings for $9.99.

An advertisement for Maggi shows a man standing in the doorway of his apartment speaking directly to the camera about never really seeing his neighbor next door. He describes running into the neighbor in the elevator, but the neighbor looks down at his phone and avoids eye contact. The man says, “I miss you buddy,” as Maggi branding appears on screen along with the hashtag #wemissyoutoo.

This Nike advertisement features a young athlete training intensely while others are still asleep, emphasizing the importance of dedication and hard work. The video follows his early morning routine, including running through quiet streets and practicing basketball drills alone on a court. A voiceover highlights his motivation to stay one step ahead of the competition through constant practice and sacrifice. The ad concludes with the Nike logo and the question, 'What's your motivation?', reinforcing the brand's message of relentless pursuit of excellence.

An advertisement for Incredible India shows a man in a suit speaking directly to the camera before cutting to a montage of a woman in India being harassed by a group of men and taken into an auto rickshaw with a driver and another man. Inside the vehicle, the man begins touching her, and she tells him to stop while calling out for help to nearby traffic. Another vehicle pulls in front of them, and a new driver gets out and confronts the man, allowing the woman to escape into his vehicle. The scene then cuts back to the man in the suit applauding the new driver in front of a small crowd for helping the woman.

An advertisment for Apple Macintosh shows a dystopian industral facility where people dressed in grey overalls march through the halls and watch a man speaking on a giant video screen. A woman in orange shorts, being chased by soldiers, runs up to the screen and throws a hammer at it, causing the screen the explode and leaving the people in the audience with the mouths agape. A voice over explains that Apple will introduce a new computer as text and company branding appears. The ad promotes the uniqueness of new Apple products and is presented with a cinematic tone.

An advertisement for a Queasy Bake Oven toy shows a family of four sitting in an upscale restaurant with two boys looking bored with the food on the table. Suddenly a dirty Chef Queasy arrives, telling them to try the food from a purple toy oven and a quick montage shows the chef cooking food that looks like dog treats, and feeding the boys who react with excitement while their mother passes out. The ad promotes embracing grossness for great tasting treats for children with a mischievous tone.

This advertisement for Finish Line features rapper Big Sean and NBA player Anthony Davis, showcasing the hard work that happens behind the scenes. The video transitions between a locker room, a dressing room, and a hallway, highlighting the athletes' and artists' preparation and personal style. It concludes with the motivational slogan, 'What's your epic finish?' to emphasize that the brand supports the journey toward achieving one's personal best.

An advertisement for Join or Die with Craig Ferguson shows a montage of talkshow footage of host Craig Ferguson interviewing people about American history and telling jokes. Craig Ferguson sits on a couch and talks to camera about what the show is about as the montage continues showing him talking to different historians, politicians, and celebrities. The ad promotes a humorous look at American history and emphasizes that it is more about interesting people.

A parody advertisement for Biscoff shows two sock puppet monsters talking about a spread for a bagel. One monster says the spread is 'made out of fucking cookies', which causes the other monster to go crazy in a montage of bizarre and obscene acts before ending up on the beach. The ad is a humorous parody of horror tropes intended to make audiences laugh at the absurdity of it.

An advertisement for Nestle shows a beautiful young woman eating a chocolate popsicle after boarding a light rail train. Romantic music plays as she notices a young attractive man and imagines his watch, wired earphones, and shirt melting away. The attraction becomes mutual when notices her shirt strap melting away as well. They exchange flirtatious eye contact, and after she finishes her ice cream, she walks away with a satisfied smile. The ad ends with promotion of the JOYA ice cream bar from Nestle with the narrator describing the ice cream bar as 'The hottest ice cream bar ever'.

An advertisement for DC shoes shows a group of skateboarders in an indoor skate park performing a variety of impossible basketball trick shots and landing them. Then, a skateboarder skates up a half-pipe and talks to camera while picking up a dog, as DC branding appears. The ad promotes the skills of the skateboarders, associating them the DC brand, and is presented in an observational and laid-back tone.

An animated advertisement for Pokémon Trading Card Game: XY—Breakpoint opens with an animated Pikachu making his familiar expression as the tagline “Gotta catch ’em all” appears behind him. An intense narrator then introduces fast-paced visuals of in-game combat between powerful Pokémon titans in an underwater setting, followed by close-ups of the featured Pokémon cards. The advertisement concludes with a shot of the card packaging and the game title, announcing that the set is available in stores now. The target audience is Pokémon fans.

An advertisement for The Law Offices of Scott Warmuth shows a man speaking to camera while mopping the floor as a second man slips and falls over in front of him. The second man starts speaking to camera and is revealed to be identical to the first man. A montage plays of various accidents - such as a car accident, knocking over a pram, and spilling coffee - with each injured party revealed to be the same man each time, eventually ending back in the office and transitioning to company branding. The ad promotes the law firms belief that they will helped everyone and is presented in a humorous tone.

The advertisement shows a man walking himself out of a hospital with his saline drip still attached on a rolling stand. He moves through the city, taking a bus, riding an elevator, and going to work, until his boss points to his watch and the man’s reality shifts back to the hospital, where he is being cared for. The man is shown lying in a hospital bed surrounded by loved ones as a representative discusses healthcare insurance options through Bharti. The ad concludes with on-screen text explaining how to purchase Bharti health insurance policies and highlighting coverage for expenses such as home and car EMIs, credit card payments, and a child’s school fees.

In a Dove commercial, Heather, a talented boxer, shares her experience of being underestimated based on her appearance. She challenges the notion that she can't be a fighter because of her looks, emphasizing that beauty and athleticism can coexist. The ad showcases her intense workout routines at the gym to convey a message of defining beauty on one's own terms, in line with the campaign slogan #MyBeautyMySay.

An advertisement for Clash of Kings shows slow motion video game footage of a medieval battle in front of a castle as a voice over gives a speech about fighting to win. Armored soldiers charge across the battlefield, a soldier stabs another with a sword, flaming arrows fly past, and a king stands on the castle wall overlooking the battle before the camera zooms out and text and product graphics are shown. The ad promotes the product as intense and dramatic with a cinematic and epic tone intended for gamers.

An advertisement shows the new dolls and play sets available based on the Monster High: Frights, Camera, Action film. The ad features close ups of the four new dolls--Clawdia, Honey, Viperine, and Elissabat--as a song plays in the background with lyrics that detail the name of each character and their role, while hands from off screen move the dolls around the toy movie set. It highlights the different ways to interact with the dolls and the play set, from the black carpet to the dressing room.

An advertisement for the Barbie Hawaiian Ice Party toy set shows two young girls using the toy to make frozen treats. The girls open a plastic pineapple container, pour ice in and use the top piece to crush it. Then, they scoop the ice into coconut-shaped cups, add flavored drink mix, and taste the finished treats while expressing approval. The ad emphasizes how fun and easy it is to make ice coolers with the set, using a bright and playful tone.

An advertisement for Skype introduces a new platform feature for group calls. The ad shows a montage of split-screen videos of people talking to one another on video chat. Different groups of people are shown discussing dinner plans, showing off a new dog, and opening gifts from relatives, all while using their phones. The footage is intercut with text graphics encouraging viewers to be creative and share memorable, spontaneous moments with one another on the go.

An advertisement for Samsung shows singer Rihanna in a sleek, futuristic environment with dramatic lighting. She performs controlled, choreographed movements as the electronic music rises and the scene becomes more intense. The video transitions to Rihanna holding a floating Samsung smartphone, surrounded by men in black streetwear. The ad presents Samsung as bold, fashionable, and futuristic.

An advertisement for 'the Barista Express' shows close up shots of a coffee making machine against a white background as it goes through the steps of brewing a coffee. A voice over explains the process, and a woman is shown talking to the camera about the machine, while footage is shown of different types of coffee being poured into mugs. The ad promotes Breville as a simple to use product that can do complicated things.

An advertisement for Quiznos shows a man enjoying a sandwich in his kitchen when the conveyor oven speaks to the man with a deep playful voice over about the food. The ad then features close ups of the sandwich from various angles, including shots of it cooking on the grill, while also emphasizing its affordable price. The man repeats the tagline 'Only 4 dollars' three times to highlight the cost. The advertisement is presented in a humorous tone.

An advertisement for Breville Smart Oven opens with a hand turning a knob on the oven to select different cooking options on the oven's digital screen. Then the ad shows a variety of foods and desserts on oven plates, each accompanied by five star reviews. This is followed by a image of the product in different sizes accompanied by its own 4 1/2 star review of the brand 'The highest rated toaster ovens'. This ad promotes the versatility of its ovens and the satisfaction of the brand as a whole.

This advertisement for the BCSPCA features clips of abused, neglected, and disabled animals, with on-screen text highlighting the number of animals abused every hour and rescued annually. Sarah McLachlan, while petting a dog, urges viewers to call and consider donating $18 a month to help animals escape abuse and receive care from the BCSPCA; donations support medical services, food, shelter, and love. Viewers who call or join online within the next 30 minutes receive a welcome kit featuring a photo of an animal being helped by their donation. Somber music plays throughout the advertisement, creating a sad tone.

An advertisement for McDonald’s features a stylish woman with long red hair wearing a Ronald McDonald-inspired outfit. She poses as the ad uses quick close-ups of her face and outfit along with close-up shots of a McGrand tomato burger and a tomato being held. A playful, upbeat jingle reminiscent of McDonald’s “I’m Lovin’ It” theme plays as McDonald’s branding appears. The ad promotes the McGrand tomato burger as a new and unique menu item in a quirky, fashion-forward tone.

This BuzzFeed advertisement titled 'Can You Watch This Without Getting Hungry?' showcases a series of high-quality, close-up shots of various savory and sweet dishes being prepared. The video features sensory-rich scenes including sizzling bacon, the assembly of a gourmet sandwich, and a bacon-wrapped steak. The second half shifts to desserts, displaying glazed donuts, cream-filled puffs, and a decadent chocolate cake. The ad uses appetizing visuals and on-screen text to engage the viewer's appetite, concluding with a call to subscribe for more content.

A commercial for the UNICEF Tap Project shows Selena Gomez in her home turning on a faucet and playfully interacting with an animated bluebird. She moves around the room in a light, whimsical way while water runs and splashes onto her hand and the floor. The perspective then shifts to a repairman working on a wall light fixture, who looks on confused by what he is seeing. The ad ends by promoting the UNICEF Tap Project in a humorous, playful tone.

An advertisement for the snack brand goodnessknows follows a man who teaches people on a city street how to play various musical instruments. Participants initially struggle and play poorly, but gradually improve as he guides them, leading to a montage of different individuals successfully playing a simple tune together. The ad finishes showing the goodnessknows snack bar with the man saying 'anybody else want try a little goodness today' serving a double entrende referencing the snack bar and the public instrument playing demonstration.

An advertisement for the 1964 presidential election shows a young girl counting the petals of a flower as a deep, echoing voice begins a countdown and the camera zooms into her eye, followed by a sudden explosion. A narrator warns of destruction if viewers do not vote and urges them to support Lyndon B. Johnson in the election on November 3. The advertisement is presented with an uneasy and ominous tone and is directed toward American voters.

An advertisement for Lay's chips shows a montage of different people at home and at work watching and following the ICC Cricket World Cup as an Indian pop song about the product plays. In the next scene, a man arrives in a classroom and presents Lay's chips to distract a professor and everyone leaves the classroom, which transitions into all of the people sitting in a living room watching the game on TV. The ad highlights the product as the official snack of the ICC Cricket World Cup and is presented in an upbeat and comical tone.

A black-and-white advertisement for Coca-Cola features actress Connie Clausen speaking directly to the camera while measuring a mannequin and joking that it once matched her figure but now has a smaller waistline. She picks up a bottle of Coca-Cola and describes its taste, low calorie content, satisfaction that helps prevent overeating, and energy-related benefits. She then returns to the mannequin and jokes that it should not get any thinner as the ad continues to reference Coca-Cola’s stated benefits. The ad is directed toward soda drinkers.

An advertisement for Game of War shows a man sitting in a busy area of Mumbai playing a game on his cell phone as miniature CGI medieval soldiers climb out of the phone. A montage is shown of different people playing the game on their phones in different locations across the world, as miniature soldiers travel across the city and end up on a snowy battlefield. A voice over says, 'join your allies, unite the world,' and the soldiers raise their swords infront dragon, as branding appears.

An advertisement for Carl’s Jr. features Padma Lakshmi walking through a market while smelling and touching various spices. She narrates her experiences with food and states that there is something distinct about the Carl's Jr.'s Western Bacon Burger.
