The ad shows her seated on the steps of an apartment building eating the burger, with sensual close-up shots of her mouth, sauce dripping from the food, and deliberate movements such as licking sauce and adjusting her clothing. The commercial ends with a Carl’s Jr. title card and the tagline “More than just a piece of meat' and is directed toward burger consumers.

An advertisement for MAC Cosmetics’ Viva Glam line features Ariana Grande in a music video–style commercial. It opens on a stylized pink portrait that animates and expands into a wall mural as retro, 1960s-inspired music plays. When Ariana appears, the music shifts to a more modern pop beat as she dances and poses, painting her initials, a heart, and “VIVA GLAM” beside the mural. The ad emphasizes a bold, youthful glam aesthetic.

The video opens with a top-down shot of an ice skater spinning against a clean ice background. It then transitions to a computer screen displaying an image of the same individual, along with his name and profession as a professional figure skater. The video showcases his personal website, featuring his 'about' page. The Squarespace logo and company name are subsequently introduced as the platform used to create the site, followed by a brief overview of its services, including website creation, domain management, and e-commerce solutions.

An advertisement for Bubble Witch 2 Saga shows a woman sitting in a park reading a magazine. She looks across the park and sees a bicycle pulling a cart with a ghost stuck in a bunch of colorful bubbles. She runs after the cart and uses a magic ring to shoot the bubbles and free the ghost, which flies over to hug her and goes through her. Graphics and branding for Bubble Witch 2 Saga appears with a prompt to download now for free.

An advertisement for a Spider-Man video game shows the Green Goblin jumping on a rooftop with a bomb in his hand and threatening Spider-Man who is playing a video game on a television. Spider-Man fails to play the game as the Green Goblin laughs at him; and Spider-Man turns to the camera and says, 'is this more action than even Spider-Man can handle?' The ad ends as branding appears for Parker Brothers..

An advertisement for Wendy's Burger opens in a Soviet fashion show where a man plays the violin and a woman in uniform announces the clothing presented. The model comes out for each option in the same outfit. The video then cuts to the narrator stating 'having no choice is no fun, that's why at Wendy's every hamburger isn't dressed the same' over images of Wendy's burgers and its fresh ingredients, showing the variety and options of Wendy's burgers.  Emphasizing that customers can choose exactly how they want their burger to be made.

An advertisement for Coca-Cola shows a man trying to order a can of soda and turning around to see a second man, who looks exactly like him, drinking a can. He tries to repeatedly steal the can and when he finally gets it, it is empty. Suddenly he is bumped into by a woman, who also looks like him, holding a bottle of Coca-Cola that the man stares at. The ad promotes the idea that Coca-Cola is desirable and people may go crazy for it, and is presented in a humorous and offbeat tone.

[*note from ZS to reviewer - I think the woman is meant to be the man dressed up as a lady because the man says the same line to her as he does to the other man...I can't tell because of the quality, but I think the joke is that every character is him...maybe? Also the man is a famous Indian actor Amir Khan, not sure if worth mentioning?]

A Buzzfeed Blue promo shows photo portraits of various women from different countries, posed in front of landscapes, and wearing clothing ascociated with their culture. Text graphics accompany the photos and promote beauty in being different, support for different cultures, and beautiy in 'being yourself.' The video is presented in an inspiring and thoughtful tone.

A Pepsi Cola advertisement for Pepsi features the story of a woman told in a storybook format. The woman is featured as a girl who eventually grows up to marry a young man. The ad features how she goes about her day, walking to stay slim, going shopping, eating lightly, staying active, and being loyal to her husband. The ad shows this journey on a stage in a continuous set, showing different flashpoints in her life and daily routine. In their living room, she brings out a Pepsi for her husband as a light, refreshing drink. The ad highlights how Pepsi Cola is part of a light, healthy diet and emphasizes its role in maintaining a lasting relationship.

An advertisement for New Yorker clothing shows a wedding between a young woman and an old man. Later on, in a huge mansion, the old man is waiting for the woman in bed, before going and looking through a keyhole as she changes clothes. She dances seductively in her underwear, which causes him to collapse. She steps over his body and goes outside, champagne glass in hand, while overlooking the sunset on her balcony. The ad promotes New Yorker clothing as designed for the "moment" and is presented in a sensual and humorous tone.

An advertisement for the Ugglys toy shows a young boy playing with an ugly dog toy and making disgusting sounds with it. The narrator explains that the toy comes with over 30 sounds and shows different scenes, like the boy using fart noises to bother his family. The commercial highlights the product’s gross-out appeal, presents it in a humorous tone, and ends by showcasing the toy’s packaging and branding. The target audience is young boys.

An advertisement for South Africa features a man traveling through the country while delivering a monologue, accompanied by uplifting music. This ad explores a variety of locations through the man's point of view, including landscape montage and interaction with tourists and locals in the field, on beaches, in the city, and in other cultural activities. He explains the profound thoughts and feelings he gains from the trip. This ad promotes tourism in South Africa in a friendly and upbeat tone, highlighting the diverse activities and the once-in-a-lifetime experience the country offers.

An advertisement for Rescue Clearwater shows a montage of people rescuing and helping marine animals on the beach, on boats, and in the ocean. The ad promotes caring for and showing respect for the natural world, which is presented in an inspiring tone.

This is a PSA by the Law Center to Prevent Gun Violence, bringing awareness to mass shootings. The ad features celebrities -- actors and athletes --  listing different mass shooting casualty events and then reading the same statement word by word, collectively urging viewers to demand political action to stop mass shooting events. The PSA has a serious tone displayed in black and white. The PSA emphasizes the need for a plan and the dissatisfaction with a lack of action on the part of the government.

An advertisement for the Atari 2600 game console shows two children playing a variety of games on the console while a man raps a song about the product in the background. It highlights the wide variety of games available on the console as well as its low price of under $50. The ad ends showcasing the gaming console and is presented in an upbeat tone for a younger audience.

A political advertisement for the campaign of Republican state representative Joe Straus shows Sheriff A. J. Louderback discussing the actions Joe Straus took in securing the United States border in Texas. The ad features the Sheriff stating that Joe Straus added troops to the border, took the fight to the drug cartels, cracked down on human trafficking, and helped to pass a ban on sanctuary cities. It highlights Straus's ability to keep Texans safe during his current term and will continue to do so if re-elected.

An advertisement for 5 Peppermint Gum opens with a man and a woman sitting side by side quietly on a couch while a crowd dances around them. The woman looks at the man, and the ad starts a five-second countdown with breathing and heartbeat sound effects. As it counts down, the woman leans towards the man and kisses him. Then a black screen appears with the logo and the tagline "life happens in 5", and ends by displaying the product. This ad promotes this peppermint gum in an optimistic tone and suggests it will give you the confidence to leap.

An advertisement for the Five Nights at Freddy's 4 video game shows a montage of gameplay footage while text asks the viewer questions, indicating the player character is at fault for the events of the game. The ad features creepy scenery inside a house and multiple strange animal figures. It highlights the scariness of the game while presented in a creepy tone.

This is an animated General Mills commercial for the Cookie Crisp cereal. The featured mascot, Chip the Wolf, preys on young children having a picnic with cookie crisp cereal. He talks to the viewer and explains his plan for stealing the Cookie Crisp by introducing a complicated contraption. The contraption seemingly works to pull away the Cookie Crisps, but then overdoes it by sending Chip around the world, eventually crashing back into the contraption, while the Cookie Crisps end up back with the children. The commercial uses lighthearted gags to emphasize that Cookie Crisps are a fun cereal to eat in the morning while aimed at a young demographic.

An advertisement for bareMinerals Blemish Remedy beauty products shows a woman with acne and blemishes applying the products while a woman narrates the benefits of the product. She claims the products will give your skin a flawless look and diminish imperfections. The ad is presented in an uplifting tone, emphasizing that skincare can be positive.

An advertisement for Peak Sweet Mother flavor shows a montage of different sons, daughters, and families singing, dancing, and embracing their mothers. A catchy song plays as the people sing along to it, intercut with food being cooked and served before Peak branding appears. The ad promotes Peak as easy to share and cook together, and is presented in a wholesome, family tone.

An advertisement for a Dunlop Cry Baby Wah guitar pedal created by John Petrucci shows close-ups of a guitar pedal in slow motion while guitarist John Petrucci speaks about the pedal. Petrucci steps on it and is revealed playing the guitar and creating the wah sound effect. The video then cuts to black as text branding appears with John Petrucci's name and a release date, "Coming February 2016." The ad promotes a unique product created by a professional musician and suggests to audiences that they can sound like him if they use it, and it is presented in an informative tone.

An advertisement for the video game Portal 2 features animation footages of robot characters, accompanied by an informative narration. It opens with an animated scene in a lab where a human pushes another human off a cliff, with the narration saying, "humans cannot be trusted, the solution, robots." Then the ad shifts to a factory that builds robots and shows them engaging in different trust exercises. By the end, a robot still pushes its teammate off the cliff, and the ad concludes by displaying the video game cases for each respective gaming console, and encouraging viewers to pre-order on the website. It promotes the game with a humorous tone, targeting gamers.

This is an advertisement for Prada, which shows ten different fashion models wearing Prada clothing. The video intercuts between each model dancing, looking pensively, throwing flowers, speaking to the camera, and doing different actions. The narrator reads a story about the ten women as the models act out each movement in cinematic frames. The video then ends with the Prada logo and announces that this line of clothing is coming in Spring and Summer of 2013.

An advertisement / anti-bullying campaign collaboration between Pacer and the video game Life Is Strange shows a montage of dramatic cutscenes from Life Is Strange. The montage shows teenagers being bullied and teased within a high school setting as a voice-over speaks about how people can send in stories about when they stood up to adversity or defended a friend in need. The video serves as a marketing piece to promote a video game about bullying and how players and fans can help in the real world, and is shown in an uplifting and hopeful tone.

An advertisement for Neckermann opens with a boy in swim trunks walking among rows of beach umbrellas and dancing to upbeat hip-hop music. He dances his way to the swimming pool, where he spots a lifeguard and makes eye contact with her, pausing his dance for a few seconds. Suddenly, the music comes back as the boy performs even more vigorous dance movements before jumping into the pool, disregarding everyone around him. This ad uses a humorous tone to promote Neckermann as the gateway to a carefree, feel-good holiday experience.

This is an advertisement for the Xbox One. In the video, Marshawn Lynch is sitting in front of a TV with a doctor who told him that he is in detention. The doctor and Lynch play Madden on Xbox One, and they banter with each other as the doctor uses the stats on the game for his fantasy football. The video then cuts to the Xbox logo and the tag line "The Evolution of Game Day," and the voiceover says "Fantasy, Highlights, Next gen stats, the NFL on Xbox One." It then adds a button with Lynch holding a raccoon before cutting to the pack shot of the Xbox, showing it only costs $349. This ad is intended for gamers, specifically young boys and men.

This is an ad for female athletes and performance underwear made for them by the [Under.me](http://Under.me) company. It shows an adult female tennis player in her undergarments on a tennis court as she trains. The ad is presented in black and white, and the underclothes are also white, which calls more attention to them. The film clips are accompanied by a casual male voiceover and a music track, which includes the jingle, "If you're feeling under pressure, these pants will keep you fresher."

An advertisement for Chickenjoy by Jollibee shows two people in a Jollibee location singing a song about the brand with a 360-degree camera angle. Eventually, everyone in the cafeteria starts doing a coordinated dance to the song with lyrics singing about how good the food is. It associates the product with extraordinary happiness associated with song and dance routines presented in an upbeat tone and ending with showcases the Chickenjoy and their slogan "Share the joy all around!"

An advertisement for Subway shows a man talking to the camera before walking into a Subway restaurant. A catchy jingle about Chicken Tandoori is played while being lip-synced by customers as they eat Subway sandwiches. Close-up shots of Subway Chicken Tandoori ingredients are shown as product branding appears. The ad is presented in a humorous and quirky tone.

This is an ad for Old El Paso that walks viewers through how to make Mexican buffalo chicken dip. It shows each ingredient step by step, including refried beans, taco seasoning, cream cheese, celery, blue cheese dressing, hot sauce, and rotisserie chicken. The tutorial demonstrates mixing all the ingredients and instructs viewers to “bake at 350 degrees for 35 minutes.” The ad ends by showcasing the finished dish and displaying the Old El Paso branding.

An advertisement for Berocca features different hands rhythmically grabbing a glass of water, popping a capsule, and dropping a tablet into the water. The actions repeat and turn into a percussive beat before graphics appear showing the Berocca packaging box and detailing the uses for the product. The ad emphasizes the tablets as refreshing and energy boosting and is shown in an informative and upbeat tone.

This is a commercial for TOD's shoes. The commercial features a well-dressed woman in red Tod shoes getting into a classic car and driving. A well-dressed man drives by and acknowledges her style. They eventually meet at a luxurious mansion, during which shots of the Tod shoes and bag are featured. The commercial emphasizes the chic style of the TOD brand.

An advertisement for the state of Colorado highlights the picturesque landscapes while a mother and daughter enjoy the scenery. The ad features a man taking in the view of a lake surrounded by a mountain range before diving into the lake as the narrator describes how nature should be enjoyed in the present moment. It highlights how life is about living, not waiting, and Colorado's landscape can offer that serenity.

An advertisement for Brisk Iced Tea features an animated version of Eminem in claymation style, explaining why he doesn't do commercials. Eminem is shown partying with girls, walking on a street, and recording his rap in a recording studio. He explains that he typically rejects other brands because he dislikes their product or the producers dislike him, but after tasting the Brisk Ice Tea, he admits, "It's pretty good." This ad promotes the drink with a dramatic and humorous tone, emphasizing the product's outstanding taste.

A political advertisement shows Trump's history with the Democrat party through a montage of televised speeches and interviews where Trump proclaimed his closeness with Democratic politicians in the past. The ad features a news segment explaining that Trump had given more money to Democrats than Republicans in the past. The ad is presented in an intense, politically charged tone.

An advertisement for Cadbury Dairy Milk Chocolate shows a male student trying to wish a girl in his class a happy Valentine's Day with a Cadbury Dairy Milk chocolate bar. The ad features the students of the class passing the note and chocolate bar across the room as each of them takes a square of chocolate for themselves, leaving only one piece for the girl who enjoys. It highlights how the chocolate can bring people together and spread joy and love to others.

This ad was made by [MLB.com](http://MLB.com), which represents Major League Baseball in the United States. It tells a passionate story through sound bites from an experienced baseball manager, who praises the beauty of the game and honors the players. The voiceover is paired with cinematic clips of players practicing, training, and laughing together. At one point, he says, "There are no Cinderellas in baseball." It ends with the website and official MLB logo. The ad emphasizes the tradition of the game while acknowledging that the future looks bright.

An advertisement for EAT24 features Snoop Dogg asking "Are you Hangry?" (a portmanteau of hungry and angry) to the viewer, intercut with Gilbert Gottfried acting out the symptoms as narrated by Snoop: yelling at random objects, having a hallucination about a pet fish that turns into sushi due to hunger. Then Snoop Dogg offers the man the EAT24 app to "shut up". It concludes with Snoop Dogg framing EAT24 as "the best way to order food online," as the logo appears on the screen. This ad uses a humorous tone to promote the app's convenience in solving hunger frustrations.

An advertisement for Kano features a girl building a computer from parts and showcases the variety of features inside the computer, accompanied by uplifting music. It demonstrates the building process step by step, with text explaining different parts and actions. The ad positions the product as "A new world of code" and lists the things you can do with the computer, including building games, making music, and creating videos. This ad uses a friendly and informative tone to promote Kano's DIY approach to technology, emphasizing how its educational tools can empower children to level up their creative skills.

This is a commercial for Cadbury Dairy Milk branded chocolate bars. The commercial opens to a tagline that reads "Cadbury Dairy Milk taste like this feels". Then it features a bear dancing alone in a forest to the song "That's The Way I Like It" by KC and the Sunshine Band. After dancing, the title card "Free the Joy" appears, emphasizing that the chocolate from Cadbury Dairy Milk tastes like joy itself.

This video features a man covered in ice cream while staring directly at the camera. The man proceeds to take a spoon and scoop ice cream onto himself and eats it. The camera zooms out slowly while the man keeps staring, eventually a graphic appears on screen "thx for watching :3"

An advertisement for an energy drink features a man walking into an office for an appointment. A security guard greets him, gives him a badge, and quickly changes into a receptionist. The receptionist runs away, changes, and poses as a secretary, offering him a drink. Finally, he rushes into the office, changes into a suit, and greets the man for his appointment. The ad humorously highlights the energy drink’s ability to handle anything.

This is a political ad for George H.W. Bush featuring charged political statements against Michael Dukakis. The ad highlights the candidate's stance on the death penalty, therefore crime itself, by declaring Bush's support and Dukakis' opposition. The ad proceeds to mention a specific example of a criminal being sentenced to life in prison instead of the death penalty, and the consequences of giving the criminal charitable benefits like weekend releases. The ad emphasizes Bush's position on the death penalty and his appeal to like-minded voters.

This is an advertisement for Thinkbox TV for TV advertising. In the video, a couple walks through a dog shelter and looks at a bunch of different dogs. They stop on dog who with a TV in its room. The dog, Harvey, taps the remote, and the TV starts playing a video montage of all the tasks it does as a pet, ending with "Every home needs a Harvey". The video ends with the couple looking perplexedly at the dog as the video cuts to the tag line "Discover the power of TV advertising at [www.thinkbox.tv](http://www.thinkbox.tv), TV. Where brands get their breaks", showing that one can advertise their brand with Thinkbox TV, like how the dog in the shelter does to potential owners.

An advertisement for Zazoo condoms shows a father and son in a store as the son keeps putting an item he wants into the cart. The ad features the father repeatedly putting the item back, which results in the kid getting upset and throwing items in the store while the father gets embarrassed. It highlights how using a condom can prevent the responsibilities someone might not be ready for while being fun, sexy, and safe.

An advertisement for Ball Mitsubishi opens with Jenifer Ball explaining her company's values. Then the ad shows a slideshow of a Mitsubishi car accompanied by a voiceover describing the affordable lease services. Later, Jenifer frames the company as being "freeway close, just minutes from downtown" to emphasize its accessibility and convenience to people in National City. It concludes with a slideshow featuring two cars and the business website. This ad promotes a local car rental service in a friendly and informative tone.

This is an ad for Microsoft's Xbox FIFA 16 game, and it features celebrity soccer players like Lionel Messi and Alex Morgan in real life as they make incredible moves in motion-capture suits, then intercuts those shots with animated versions of the same players from within the game, replicating the moves we just saw in real life. The ad also shows amateur soccer players in informal neighborhood locations around the world as they dribble the ball and then pass it off-frame to a player who lives somewhere else. The end message from EA Sports and Microsoft is to "Buy Xbox One and get FIFA 16".

A game trailer for the PlayStation 2 video game SmackDown, featuring a montage of live and in-game action versions of the wrestlers. It highlights scenes of wrestlers bursting through the stadium doors, smackdowns in the ring, parking lot fights, and female wrestler panty matches. The ad posits that this is non-stop action video game entertainment, ending with a promotion of the video game.

This Public Service Announcement from The Voice of Nature group urges viewers to advocate for the inclusion of biodiversity preservation in the Paris Agreement at the upcoming COP21 Summit. The ad features Koko, a gorilla who uses sign language to highlight the importance of protecting our planet. A call to action follows Koko, encouraging viewers to sign the online petition supporting [Koko.org](http://Koko.org). The PSA emphasizes the need to listen to nature by having a direct advocate, Koko.

This is an animated Ubisoft commercial promoting animated shorts based on the video game Hungry Shark. The commercial features different sharks wearing shades, then a hammerhead shark who can't quite wear shades in the same way due to the placement of its eyes. The hammerhead shark proceeds to try different manually constructed ways to affix the shades to its eyes, finally succeeding in a silly, poorly constructed way. Rain falls, ruining the success of the moment, and the hammerhead shark goes away. The commercial promotes the silliness of the shark characters and promises more adventures via short commercials in the final tag line.

This is a Remco commercial for the "Baby Laugh A Lot" doll. The commercial features little girls playing with the toy by rocking its chair and pressing a button in the center that causes the baby to laugh maniacally. As the baby laughs, so do the little girls, and the narrator seemingly has no control. The commercial emphasizes the baby laugh a lot toy ability to spread its laughter contagiously.

This is a commercial for the mobile game Candy Crush. The ad features a woman at a bus stop who sees Candy Crush sodas in real life. She decides to match the colors in a row, causing them to burst and spawn other candy crush shapes and sodas all across the city. Random people turn into candy and match colors and burst, causing a repeat-bursting soda effect. The commercial ends with a call to action to download the Candy Crush app, emphasizing that anyone can play at anytime for free.

This ad is for the chocolate brand Dairy Milk. The ad shows a couple eating dinner at the dinner table when the woman asks the man when he last time he said I love you to her. He then gets up and takes a Dairy Milk chocolate bar out of the refrigerator and hands it to her. The ad then cuts to the chocolate pieces from the bar on a plate with the tagline "Meethe mein kuch meetha ho jaaye".

This is a commercial for Jack in the Box featuring its live-action mascot. Jack walks down a street as he addresses the audience directly about the all-day convenience of his menu, highlighting that competitors only offer certain items at certain times of day. The ad ends with Jack ripping off his sleeves, showing his muscles, and declaring in front of a Burger King that if there is a problem, they can take it up with him. The commercial emphasizes Jack in the Box's rebellious nature as the preferred choice for food at any time of the day.

An advertisement for Sony Bravia set in a large urban housing compound with large buildings surrounding a grassy area. The ad features multi-angle shots with a large paint explosion synchronized to a classical music track. The paints explode up and along the façades, rippling across with intense rainbow colors. A clown is shown running across the green before a climax, a colorful explosion fills the scene, and the façades of the buildings are covered with paint falling everywhere. The ad highlights how Sony Bravia televisions can visualize and transmit the most incredible image and color quality for televisions. The tone is dramatic and exciting.

An advertisement for Nespresso set in a hotel where two hotel guests get their luggage mixed up. The ad features George Clooney and a woman opening their respective suitcases in separate rooms and realizing they have inadvertently switched their luggage; both have Nespresso in them, but the wrong clothing. They meet in the lobby to exchange luggage, where the woman also hands George his sleep mask. The ad highlights how even perfect strangers have the same taste because the product is so good. The tone of the ad is flirtatious and playful.

A public service announcement for quitting smoking by the Health Promotion Board. The ad features a woman talking about the dangers of smoking. It features a close-up of the woman's face as she speaks on oral cancers, while large sores and abscesses are visible around her mouth and gums. She challenges the viewer that if looking at the pictures of cancers on the cigarette box makes you uncomfortable, look at the warning label for the hotline for quitting smoking. The tone is ominous and serious and is directed at people who smoke.

An advertisement for Assassin's Creed Identity shows a man in a white hoodie walking through a tunnel playing the game on his smartphone. A montage of in-game footage is shown, highlighting the gameplay mechanics and action set pieces of a hooded assassin in a Renaissance setting. The man exits the tunnel and sees a reflection of himself as the hooded assassin in a car window before product branding appears. The ad promotes the game as action-packed and is presented in a cinematic and informative tone.

An advertisement for Coloria Italiana shows a woman doing laundry when a slobby, dorky white man in tighty-whities appears and tries to seduce her. She throws him into the laundry machine, sitting atop it until the laundry cycle ends, as product branding for Coloria is shown. Afterwards, the laundry opens to reveal a muscly and attractive black man, which excites the woman, as text graphics appear saying "coloured is better" and the man poses. The ad is presented in a humorous, if a bit tongue-in-cheek, tone.

An advertisement for Banglalink opens with a warm, celebratory, and cinematic tone through Bollywood-style storytelling. The visuals focus on a joyful wedding, family members preparing food, dancing, and sharing memorable moments. Bright colors, traditional clothing, and festive music create a sense of togetherness. The mood is energetic, heartfelt, and emphasizes connections across generations. The ad concludes with a posed family wedding photo and a Banglalink logo, reinforcing themes of shared moments and staying connected.

An advertisement for Doritos featuring Logan Paul and a friend walking through a hallway with a packet of Doritos when the lights go out, and a ghoul appears before them, a lá "Lights Out," and tries to snatch the Doritos away. Logan Paul asserts he won't give the ghoul the Doritos, causing the ghost to attack the two friends and send them flying away with paranormal abilities. The ad is presented in a humorous tone.

An advertisement for !ndigo shows a young boy passing a note to a girl in a classroom when a teacher catches him and reads the note aloud to the class. The note reads like a poem where the boy professes romantic interest in the girl, and the teacher looks impressed as the girl smiles at the boy before a text graphic appears saying "reading inspires kids." The ad promotes supporting education and teaching kids about reading and writing, and is presented in a wholesome tone.

An advertisement for Poochare shows a man in a retro blue suit with a dog stepping out of a car and shopping at a grocery store as women look lustfully at him, like hungry animals. A catchy jingle plays before cutting to a dog eating from a bowl and wearing retro-visors. The ad promotes Poochare as a brand that is high-class and that people are envious of, and is presented in a humorous tone.

This is a Coca Cola Commercial featuring the Coke Zero campaign. The commercial describes the intent and motivation behind the Coke Zero campaign, spotlighting the execution of key marketing concepts behind the "drinkable campaign". By showing people Shazam Coke Zero commercials, simulating people drinking Coke Zero from a billboard, and transforming merchandise into straws and cups. The commercial ends with the tagline "Drink an ad," emphasizing the uniqueness of the Coke Zero Campaign and associating that with Coke Zero itself.

A trailer for the movie 10 Cloverfield Lane shows a woman getting in a car crash and waking up in a man's room, played by John Goodman. She escapes from him and finds a house emitting strange lights from its windows. The trailer highlights the mysterious aspect of the movie by not explaining anything; it shows building suspense in the viewer and the stakes for the character in the movie. The trailer is followed by a call to action to see the movie in theaters.

An advertisement for the video game Paragon shows a montage of fantasy gameplay footage over intense electronic music. Battles are shown between science-fiction and fantasy characters - both human and monsters -shooting weapons and using magical powers in slow motion across a mountainous battlefield. The gameplay showcases several playable characters, each with unique combat abilities, and highlights the variety of styles to appeal to gamers, before text and branding appears encouraging players to "join the fight." The ad is presented in an exciting and action-packed tone.

This is a Public Service Announcement that encourages American teens to quit smoking. It shows three teens in different environments: a high school, a bedroom, and a dining room. Each teen explains the stressful situation or reason that led them to start smoking, saying lines such as: “I just can’t deal,” “Sometimes friends are jerks,” “Because they just don’t get it,” and “Because tests stress me out.” The ad wraps up with the narrator saying, "Smoking won't change that," enticing viewers to quit by texting the number 47848 to quit or visit [teen.smokefree.gov](http://teen.smokefree.gov).

An advertisement for an Indian condom company shows a man and woman arriving at an apartment and embracing each other sensually as the man takes out a condom packet and accidentally drops it down a huge spiral staircase. The man chases the packet down the stairs, engaging in slapstick-style accidents with people walking up the stairs, before eventually catching the packet as an old couple looks at him with a judgmental expression, before laughing. The ad promotes practicing safe-sex and going the extra mile to ensure it, and is presented in a comedic tone.

This is a commercial for Beados Gems, gel-like beads that join together when introduced to water. The commercial features young girls playing with the beads and creating different crafts from necklaces and bracelets to different shapes. A narrator talks about the features and explains how the Beados work by combining with water, and also lists the price and different add-ons available. The commercial emphasizes the creativity and convenience of the Beados and its targeted at young girls.

This commercial for the Clash of Kings mobile game features gameplay intercut with game cinematics while an in-game narrator monologues about power and Kings, speaking to the conquest themes of the game. The commercial ends with a "Clash of Kings" title card next to different mobile platform options, emphasizing the various ways to get started in Clash of Kings and the tagline "UNITED WE FIGHT!"

A Nintendo advertisement for the Super Smash Bros. game features 4 people costumed as Nintendo IP characters, Donkey Kong, Mario, Yoshi, and Pikachu skipping together hand in hand in a sunflower field. Lighthearted music plays, and suddenly Mario trips Yoshi, causing a chaotic free-for-all brawl between them. Later, the ad cuts to a quick montage of the actual gameplay with those characters, accompanied by a narration introducing the game. The ad promotes this game and emphasizes its four-player feature in a humorous tone, targeting gamers.

An advertisement for Viagra features a woman lying on her side in lingerie while a pale, scraggly, and bald old man starts dancing in front of her. The man starts doing breakdance spins on the floor using his erect member for balance, which impresses the woman, before a voice-over announces "the power of Viagra." The video is presented in a humorous and adult-oriented tone.

An advertisement for the [BuiltWithChocolateMilk.com](http://BuiltWithChocolateMilk.com) campaign shows slow-motion, black-and-white footage of basketball player Kevin Love, walking onto a basketball court and shooting hoops, while his voiceover comments on his technique and drive to play the sport well, concluding with him assuring he drinks chocolate milk when training and ending on a shot of a chocolate milk bottle in color. The ad is presented in an inspirational tone.

An advertisement for the Sonic Mania video game shows a montage of gameplay from a variety of past Sonic games while energetic electronic music plays. The ad features text explaining that Sonic has been going forward for his entire history by showing Sonic gameplay, but the time has come for him to go back to the past, finally revealing Sonic Mania's retro-inspired gameplay. It highlights the game as a throwback to the earliest Sonic games, presented in a fast-paced, upbeat tone.

A PSA for anti-smoking shows an old woman talking to the camera. She tells the audience in a gruff voice that people "say nicotine isn't addictive" before picking up a cigarette and using a hole in her neck to puff from it, from which smoke exits. The PSA is presented in a serious and grim tone.

An April Fool's Day prank advertisement for Google's self-driving bike in the Netherlands features a mix of interviews and footage of bikes and transportation in the Netherlands. First, the ad shows interviews with Google employees and engineers, explaining the project background and technology behind the product, while demonstrating the bike's features. Then the ad shifts to interviews with the Mayor and Netherland residents to further discuss the bike's application. It concludes by showing tw children riding the bike joyfully without a guardian to emphasize its safety and trustworthiness. This ad employs a professional and informative tone to deliver an April Fools' prank regarding a fictional high-tech product.

This ad for Tab Cola features a woman walking on the beach in a bathing suit, holding a can of the drink. A song praises the drink in the background. The ad alternates between the woman and a cup of Tab being filled with cola. The woman passes a man who is star-struck by her while drinking his own Tab cola. The ad ends with a full glass of Tab and the tagline “Great taste. Low Calorie.” The target audience is health-conscious individuals who enjoy soft drinks.

This ad is about the gum brand Orbit. The ad starts with a still frame of a man and woman shoulder-to-shoulder sitting atop a desk with an on-screen test displaying "Dirty Mouth Test 37". Then another woman enters, his wife, and all three of them get into a heated argument, and instead of exchanging foul language, they use substitute words that sound like the original curse words. Finally, the Orbit gum spokeswoman pops into frame holding the new Orbit raspberry mint gum, and states the tagline "For a good clean feeling, no matter what."

An advertisement for ESPN SportsCenter shows a tour group walking through a facility while a guide speaks, and at the back of the group, football players and brothers Peyton and Eli Manning muck around. As the tour group walks on, a man looks back at Peyton and Eli as they push each other around, and branding appears as they walk away, "This is SportsCenter". The ad is presented in a dry-humored tone.

This is an HGTV commercial for Wayfair wall decoration products. The commercial serves primarily as a tutorial showing the viewer how to add variety and style to a wall by making it a gallery wall. The featured host, Peyton Lambton, walks the viewer step by step in planning and then executing a gallery wall, referring to clocks, letters, mirrors, and signs as items that can be purchased from [wayfair.com](http://Wayfair.com). After presenting design rules to the viewer, Peyton performs a call to action while [wayfair.com](http://wayfair.com) graphic displays on screen, scrolling through different decorative items. The commercial emphasizes that Wayfair can be a place to find what you need and a place to receive genuine advice or tips for home improvement.

An advertisement for Minute Maid juice shows a woman approaching a man and saying she thinks he's the father of one of her kids. He immediately assumes she's talking about a biological child, and starts talking about a sexual encounter from his past, disturbing the woman and leading to an awkward social interaction. The narrator of the ad says, "Someone forgot to boost." A repeat of the encounter shows the woman approaching the man, but this time he's drinking from the Minute Maid juice. Now he understands that she's referring to kids in a class, as she's a teacher, and that his daughter is in her class. The ad highlights the benefits the juice has for the brain. while presented in a humorous, tongue-in-cheek tone.

This is a Microsoft commercial promoting the Xbox One console and exclusive video game properties. The commercial features different game cinematics and narration from the lead characters of the Xbox franchises like Halo, F1, Gears of War, and Tomb Raider. The narration touches on topics of individualism and pushing yourself to the limit, metaphorically asking the viewer if they will jump in like the franchise characters. The tagline Jump Ahead appears, followed by an Xbox and Microsoft logo.

An advertisement for Victoria's Secret shows a behind-the-scenes video of supermodels Elsa Hosk, Jas Tookes, and Martha Hunt wearing activewear and working out in a warehouse. The three girls address the camera individually - giving their testimony on the activewear they're wearing by highlighting their colorful sports bras and pants - intercut with images of them training with gym equipment. The ad promotes Victoria's Secret as a stylish brand for use at the gym and is presented in an upbeat tone.

An advertisement for Jack In The Box shows the company's founder, Jack (shown wearing an oversized head of the Jack in the Box's mascot), returning to business after being fired and blown up. The ad features Jack walking into the elevator and making his way to the company's boardroom before blowing it up in favor of making the company better than ever. It highlights that Jack In The Box is at its best when it showcases its original ideas and cuisines.

An advertisement for San Diego State University features an interview with Bryan Ransom, the director of athletic bands at the university. Bryan sits on a red chair and regales about his teaching background and music background. He then shares his experience as a DJ and his go-to Starbucks order. This ad makes the interview with Bryan engaging and personal, and it uses a friendly tone to promote the university.

An advertisement for Snickers shows a man painting the endzone of a football field. He accidentally misspells "CHIEFS" as "CHEFS." The narrator then says, "Not going anywhere for a while? Grab a Snickers." It highlights Snickers as an accompaniment to boring situations. The ad is presented in a humorous tone.

An advertisement for Snickers shows a group of men playing soccer in the park when a man flops after a tackle and pretends to be injured. Suddenly, a tank appears out of nowhere and crashes its way into the park before opening up to reveal Mr. T, who criticizes the man and throws a Snickers chocolate at him and tells him to "get some nuts!", the ad's tagline. The ad is presented in a humorous tone.

This is a PSA from the Centers for Disease Control promoting anti-smoking and tobacco sentiment featuring a woman who suffered from throat cancer. The commercial opens with the woman sitting outside a house, talking about her experience and expectations of smoking. While answering questions, she uses an electrolarynx device, which emphasizes the consequences of her smoking as she talks about her journey with cancer. She states she didn't expect the consequences of smoking to happen to her when she was in her 30's as the CDC logo fades in over black. The PSA emphasizes the consequences of smoking by having the woman relay her experiences in her own voice to the audience.

An advertisement for Victoria's Secret shows a montage of scantily clad supermodels in lingerie as they strut and pose in slow motion. Rock music plays as the women pose in various locations, and text graphics appear saying "what is sexy?" before company branding is shown. The ad promotes Victoria's Secret as cool, stylish, elegant, and sexy, and is presented in a cinematic tone.

An advertisement for Coca-Cola shows singer/actor Tyrese stepping onto a bus and singing a bluesy melody as he makes his way to his seat. He sees a woman sitting in front of him holding a bottle of Coca-Cola, and ends his melody by singing "always Coca-Cola", as the company logo appears. The ad promotes Coca-Cola as relaxing and enjoyable in all places, including the bus, and is presented in a lighthearted tone.

An advertisement for Brew Garden opens with basketball player Timofey Mozgov sweeping the food from another restaurant and a table tent with the text "Competitor" off the table. He then comments on Brew Garden as having "fabulous food and fine spirits" and regards this restaurant as his "home away from home". It ends with a close-up of the restaurant's logo with contact info as the narration saying "now hiring both locations." This ad uses a humorous tone to promote this restaurant and encourage people to be a part of it.

An ad for Minute Maid home-style orange juice that is made for Korean consumers. The ad features the father figure and his three delighted and thirsty young children. The ad features the family in their kitchen and then cuts to a larger-than-life animated display as the dad shows the kids how an orange is squeezed down before their eyes and becomes a glass of orange juice. The tagline, "yum yum yum," is sung by the children.

This is a Knorr commercial featuring their Fiesta Sides - Spanish rice recipe mix in a tutorial for a Hearty Chicken Chili & Rice meal. The commercial shows the steps in preparing the recipe, from cutting and cooking the chicken, preparing vegetables, and finally adding the rice recipe to the meal to complete the stir-fry. The commercial then displays the shopping list required for the recipe and features the Fiesta Sides recipe mix.

A PSA by NCADA against heroin opens with a girl consuming the drug and shows what happened to her. The girl first acts absent-minded in cheerleading, then she throws away her notebook, goes to a bar, ignores her mom's phone call, leaves her dog while walking it, and throws her clothes on the ground. Sentimental music plays as its lyrics explain the girl's condition, and the video ends with the narration, "Pick up heroin, and you will throw away anything you love." This ad promotes against heroin usage and emphasizes the negative impact of heroin on people's daily lives.

The ad is for Squarespace. It opens in a dark warehouse where a man uses a blowtorch to ignite cursive lettering ablaze on a tiled metal surface. A transparent computer screen appears in the center of the frame with the words "You Should" centered and switches to a solid black background, changing the word to fade in thin white cursive. The word scrolls to the left and reappears in flames. The ad ends with the Squarespace logo, emphasizing that Squarespace is the way to show off unique creativity.

An advertisement for Tuc biscuits shows a motorcycle rider arriving at a gas station and meeting a goat. He then plays pool with the goat, gets a tattoo of the goat on his arm, and takes the goat riding in a makeshift sidecar on his motorcycle. The ad features a song about Tuc biscuits in German that plays over the course of the whole video. The ad is presented in a humorous tone.

This advertisement shows a man explaining the features of a new Mahindra truck model. He is seen walking alongside the truck, expressing the desirable features while different points of view of the truck are presented: him walking alongside it, sitting inside, and standing in front. This ad is made to express why business owners should invest in the new Mahindra Blazo smart truck.

A cinematic trailer for the fantasy role-playing game, Seven Knights, produced by the NetMarble company. It highlights various battle scenes between the forces of good and evil, with an environment that features castles, sword fights, magical weapons, and vast landscapes, all set to a heavy metal soundtrack. The ending call to action urges the audience to download the game while displaying the various app stores where the game is available.

An ad for Jollibee shows a man, YouTuber Wil, in front of an orange background holding and talking about Super Cheese flavor french fries. The video is pushed aside into a split screen where a woman, YouTuber Janina, stands in front of a green background and holds and talks about Sour Cream flavor french fries. Colorful graphics are displayed as other people join them on each side, asking to try the fries before text appears, asking viewers to vote for which flavor they prefer. The ad promotes Jollibee with an interactive and celebrity-endorsed campaign for audiences to take part in, encouraging them to purchase each flavor, and is presented in a lighthearted tone.

An advertisement for Amazon.in shows a boy and his parents deciding how to furnish their home. It begins with the mother and the son looking at an empty wall before the mother opens the Amazon app and shows a painting that can fit on the wall that the boy approves of. Next, the father shows the boy a TV on the app and points to the same wall. As the parents continue browsing more products, they imagine various items in the house, such as a toaster, mixer, and chandelier. The ad concludes by showcasing a wide variety of home and kitchen products to highlight the vast selection available on the app. The ad suggests the user satisfaction that Amazon can bring and is presented in a lighthearted tone.

An SNL sketch parodies a political ad featuring testimonials from a variety of people who support Donald Trump. It begins with the narrator addressing the media's negative comments about Donald Trump, presenting the testimonials as the thoughts of real Americans. The people giving the testimonials all say innocuous things, but visually, it slowly reveals them all to be Nazis, Klansmen, and White Supremacists, respectively. It then reveals itself as a "Racists for Donald Trump" satire video. The video is presented in a humorous, politically charged tone.

This is a Public Service Announcement encouraging viewers to "stand up in your school" against bullying and harassment. This ad uses an adult workplace scenario to show that, regardless of age and environment, bullying is not acceptable or moral. An adult male humiliates his male colleague and even physically pushes him to the floor as he calls him names. The ad asks, "What will you do to stop bullying?" before ending message text states, "Not in our School", and includes the website [niot.org](http://niot.org).

An animated advertisement for Talking Tom Gold Run features five animal characters chasing a robber. Upbeat music plays as the three cats and two dogs characters celebrate the opening of a building, then a robber breaks through the window and drives away. The main characters start to chase the car on a street; some of them are running, jumping off a car roof, and flying in a rocket, but they fail to catch the thief and let him run away. Then the ad shows footage of actual gameplay accompanied by narrations that further explain a variety of game features. This ad promotes this game and emphasizes the excitement the game brings, targeting young gamers.

This commercial is for Purina Friskies cat food and presented by Buzzfeed. The commercial features a kitten -- whose voice is narrated by an implied adult cat who reads a letter to the younger kitten. From the point of view of the adult cat, they teach the kitten about the many idiosyncrasies that humans perform while going to the bathroom, such as using toilet paper, opening the toilet seat, etc. This narration plays while the kitten interacts with the different facets of the bathroom and eventually falls asleep in a shoe. The narrator says they should enjoy being young and appreciate the time as a kitten. The commercial is a parody of elders giving wisdom to the youth and is delivered in a sincere, lighthearted tone, emphasizing that Friskies cat food is a part of the genuine wisdom for a fulfilled kitten/cat life.

An advertisement for Subway shows two women sitting in a Subway restaurant as one woman tells the other about the sub of the day. The woman looks impressed with the options, and the pair laugh, and quick close-up shots of different daily subs are shown. The ad promotes Subway as having many different varieties for different people, and is presented in a lighthearted tone.

An advertisement for Benefit Cosmetics eyelash makeup shows a woman blowing out candles on her birthday cake when her fake eyelash catches on fire. Text then appears saying: "Keep it real." It highlights the realness of the brand's makeup product compared to others. The ad is presented in a humorous tone and ends with text saying "Laughter is the best cosmetic!" with their logo.

This is a commercial for Maxwell Cassette tapes featuring the UDI & II Hi Beam Sound version. The commercial features 3 different 30-second spots, each of which plays a pop song and features 2 actors lip-syncing to the songs with different set themes. One has the actors flying above clouds, the other features them being painted in graffiti-like visual effects, and the last features them dancing in sync. The commercials emphasize the sound quality of the cassettes as high-quality and suitable for any music preference.

An anti-drug PSA for "abovetheinfluence.com" shows a young woman sitting on a couch as a man offscreen addresses her and her friend, Sarah. The other girl explains Sarah's lack of response by stating Sarah hasn't been the same since she started smoking pot, and the camera turns to reveal Sarah as a rubbery, deflated balloon-like person. The ad promotes staying away from drugs as they will make you feel deflated, not like your old self, and be boring to be around; it is presented in a serious and informative tone.

This is an advertisement for Continental Cup, a Soup. The video opens with a grilled cheese sandwich on a kitchen counter, and the VO of the sandwich complains about being alone. Then a cup is pushed into the scene, revealing it to be a Cup a Soup filled with tomato soup. The Cup a Soup and the sandwich sing a duet about how good they go together as the video cuts to demo shots of tomatoes, soup, and sandwiches. The video ends with a pack shot of the Continental Cup, a Soup and sandwiches on a counter, and the tagline "Flavours that make your sandwich sing" appears, showing that the Cup a Soup goes great with grilled cheese sandwiches.

An advertisement for Cadbury Dairy Milk chocolate shows a gorilla playing drums to Phil Collins' "In the Air Tonight." The camera slowly pans out as the gorilla psyches himself up to play the drum solo section of the song before cutting to the packaging of Cadbury Dairy Milk chocolate with the tagline, "A glass and a half full of joy." The ad promotes the joy of having Cadbury chocolate, which is comparable to rocking out to music, and is presented in a whimsical and humorous tone.

A promo for the show Join or Die with Craig Ferguson shows a montage of Craig Ferguson interviewing diverse celebrity guests and talking about history and historical figures humorously. The montage features humorous takes from the show, debating with his guests about the Mayflower, JFK, Al Capone, and who was the worst president. The ad highlights how intellectually stimulating and rambunctious this show is, highlighted by its fast-paced and witty tone.

An advertisement for Pepsi features the boy band One Direction and NFL quarterback Drew Brees in a backstage greenroom from *The Tonight Show*. Harry Styles takes the last can of Pepsi from a cooler as Drew Brees attempts to claim it, and the other band members appear and say that music deserves the Pepsi by holding an award and a Billboard magazine while fans cheer behind them. Drew responds by displaying a championship ring and trophy, with sports fans appearing behind him. The playful standoff ends on stage, where Drew sings off-key into a microphone. The ad promotes Pepsi as a shareable product and is presented in a humorous tone.

An advertisement for Mountain Dew shows a man pressing a car-remote key fob while pointing it at another man, whose appearance changes with each press of the button. The second man suddenly develops breasts and reacts in confusion before transforming into an attractive woman in a tank top and a denim miniskirt. She asks if the man "wants a Dew?" while holding a white cup, which, on the last button press, turns the cup into a Mountain Dew bottle, much to the man's enjoyment. The ad promotes Mountain Dew as quirky and is presented in an offbeat and humorous tone. The target audience is young heterosexual men.

An advertisement for tourism in Hawaii targeted to a Japanese audience shows a montage of characters from the Ultraman franchise as they experience the different sights of Hawaii - exploring volcanoes, golfing, surfing, and the various resorts on offer. The commercial ends with a freeze frame on the beach as Japanese text graphics appear alongside a weblink. This commercial uses the Ultraman characters touring Hawaii to promote cultural exchange between the Japanese and Hawaiian people and is presented in a humorous tone.

An advertisement for Cadbury Dairy Milk Medley shows home video footage of a cat massaging a dog, before an animated chocolate bar and Cadbury branding are shown. The ad promotes Cadbury as relaxing and enjoyable and is presented in a relaxed and lighthearted tone.

An advertisement for the Euro Millions National Lottery showing a large-scale military-style paintball assault on a tropical island. The ad features men arriving by helicopter and jet skis, rappelling into a jungle, ambushing one another with paint guns, emerging from the river getting shot, and competing to capture a yellow flag. The final scene shows all the men walking toward the camera in a celebratory manner as on-screen text reads "There are millionaires. Then there are EuroMillionaires". The ad highlights how people who become millionaires are made by the National Lottery in the UK. The tone of the high-energy action is lighthearted humor.

An advertisement for sWheat Scoop cat litter shows green pawprints on the floor as the camera pans up to reveal a mouse hole, which fades into an orange and white cat walking across the floor, leaving green pawprints. A product image of cat litter appears as a voice-over asks, "How green is your cat's footprint?" The ad promotes the cat food as natural and organic, using the green footprint verbage in relation to cats, and is presented in a lighthearted tone.

A PS4 advertisement shows two young men hanging out as characters in different video game worlds. Features include two men singing "Just a Perfect Day" engaged in a medieval battle, a high-speed race on a highway where one of the cars gets flipped into the air, and a sci-fi action game in a futuristic urban warfare scene where they engage in a heavy battle. The ad highlights how just hanging out together playing games on the PS4 can be the most fun anyone can have. The ad is presented in a fast-paced, exciting tone with young men as its primary audience.

A political ad supporting President Obama's Jobs Plan in Congress. It features Obama giving a speech about Americans living paycheck to paycheck and needing help now, not fourteen months from now. The ad includes information on the American Jobs Act and urges Congress members to vote for it through Obama's passionate speech delivery.

A PSA for Sum of Us shows a man and woman sitting on a couch and meeting over a bowl of Doritos. A montage plays of the couple's relationship and them enjoying Doritos through important life milestones, eventually deciding to go on a Doritos Adventure to the Doritos Forest, where it is suddenly revealed that the forest has been cut down. Text graphics appear saying that Doritos and its parent company, Pepsico, are responsible for deforestation to obtain palm oil. The ad portrays Doritos in a negative light and is presented initially in a lighthearted tone, then shifting to a more serious, pessimistic tone.

An advertisement for Berlitz Language courses shows an older male Coast Guard instructing a young Coast Guard, both German, on how to use an emergency radio. A Mayday call comes in, reporting they are sinking, and the young Coast Guard asks, "What are you sinking about?" before branding appears and text saying, "Improve your English." The ad emphasizes that understanding language is key to effective communication and is presented in a humorous tone.

An advertisement for the Samsung Galaxy S5 shows different people using the Samsung Galaxy S5. A voice-over talks about the features of the phone as a montage plays showing people watching a movie on its screen, playing in the pool, taking pictures, running in the park, and going to dinner with friends. The ad shows that Samsung is for everyday users in everyday situations, and is presented in an informative tone.

This ad promotes the NBA. It features a video clip from a live game between the New York Knicks and Utah Jazz in the 3rd Quarter. Knicks player Jamal Crawford steals the ball, dribbles to the other end of the court, and makes a dramatic move to the basket, scoring with a layup as the crowd cheers. The message is that the NBA is full of amazing moments. The tag line at the end is "Where Amazing Happens", paired with the official NBA logo of a player in silhouette dribbling a basketball.

An advertisement for Knorr Crispy Fried Chicken Mix shows two boys and a mother watching a commercial for fried chicken on the television. The mother asks if they want fried chicken, and a montage plays of fried chicken being breaded, before the mother returns and gives the fried chicken to the boys, which they eat excitedly. The ad promotes the product as easy to use and quick to cook, and is presented in a lighthearted, family-oriented tone.

An advertisement for the mobile game Summoner's War shows cinematic footage of dragon heads in a cave as text graphics say "evil has been resurrected." The dragon bursts out of the ground, and it is revealed to have three heads, as chibi-style anime characters appear and prepare for battle with swords and magic powers. The dragon breathes fire as branding appears for Summoner's War. The ad promotes an action-packed and epic fantasy game and is shown in a cinematic tone.

An advertisement for Nike shows a montage of women at the gym, running in the park, and exercising at home, while voice over of their inner thoughts is heard. The women are heard judging themselves, their technique, comparing themselves to others, or saying they are not strong enough, but as the montage continues, they eventually get past the doubts and succeed, as text appears saying "better for it" and Nike branding appears. The ad promotes Nike as a brand for women who strive to be the best and never give up, and is presented in an inspirational tone. This specific Nike ad is targeted towards women.

An advertisement for Zenni Optical's North Coast Collection shows a montage of people in Northern California landscapes wearing different models of eyewear. A folksy song plays over slow-motion scenes of a man playing guitar on a cabin porch, a man and a woman walking through wildflower fields, a man walking barefoot, and two young women sitting on a bench in the forest. The ad highlights how the collection aligns with the outdoor lifestyle of Northern California and is presented in a feel-good tone.

An advertisement for ICICI Bank shows a child in a small village leaving school to buy candy from a grumpy man. The child returns a second time, and the grumpy man reluctantly serves her again. The child returns a third time with a friend, but lost their money on the way to the store. Disappointed, they walk away sadly, but are stopped by the grumpy man, who gives the two children candy for free. The ad emphasizes ICICI Bank as a bank that rewards customer loyalty even through unexpected challenges and is presented in a wholesome tone.

An advertisement for Game of War shows a medieval world where a beautiful warrior queen, portrayed by Kate Upton, reacts to a siege on her city. Knights and monsters do battle, and fireballs crash through the palace, as she puts on armor and rides through the battlefield on horseback, surrounded by her army. The ad promotes the Game of War as action-packed and epic, using seduction to entice the player to join, and is presented in a cinematic tone to gamers, specifically young men.

An advertisement by the National Retail Federation for small businesses in Kentucky shows a montage of people speaking to the camera intercut with different small business stores. The interviewees speak about the hardworking and supportive community, while B-roll shots show workers in stores and factories with customers smiling. Still photos and video are shown of different store items, including t-shirts, whiskey bottles, artworks, as well as Kentucky streets and outdoor statues. The ad shows a close-knit community that supports each other, and is presented in a lighthearted, optimistic tone.

This is a vintage PSA promoting a drug-free America featuring a teenager and his father. The father confronts his son with a box revealing drugs inside, asking him where he learned how to secure and hide his drugs. The teenager stammers but then reveals that he learned how do those things from watching his father. Stunned, the father looks away, and the narrator utters the tagline "Parents who use drugs have kids who use drugs". The PSA emphasizes that all behavior is learned and that if the viewer wants Americans to be drug-free, then adults and kids alike need to set that example themselves.

An advertisement for Calvin Klein Jeans shows a woman (Brooke Shields) posing and whistling while wearing jeans and boots. The camera tracks back to reveal her full body, whereupon she looks at the camera and claims nothing gets between her and her Calvins before branding appears. The ad is presented in a mysterious, stylish, and slightly seductive tone.

An advertisement for Emirates shows a group of stewardesses on a football pitch performing a mock pre-flight routine before performing football tricks and kicking goals. The crowd initially looks confused, but after the women display their football skills, the crowd starts cheering as they would in a regular match. Branding appears to show Emirates as a sponsor for the football tournament. The ad emphasizes Emirates as a passionate sponsor and that its staff are all skilled in unexpected ways.

A campaign video for Tim Pawlenty shows a montage of American iconography as a voice-over talks about the history of the country from a patriotic viewpoint. The video images range from historic moments and figures, such as Martin Luther King, tearing down the Berlin Wall, an American flag, the Statue of Liberty, and landing on the moon - intercut with Tim Pawlenty giving speeches to a crowd and greeting diverse groups of American citizens. The video is presented in a patriotic tone aimed to convince voters to support Pawlenty's views on free speech and a patriotic America, and is shown in an inspiring tone.

An advertisement for Old Milwaukee beer shows actor and comedian Will Ferrell walking toward the camera through a field of yellow flowers as inspiring fanfare music plays in the background. As he reaches the foreground of the frame, someone off-screen throws him a beer, which he catches and opens while the company logo appears. Will Ferrell starts to speak, and just as he does, the advert cuts to black. The ad is presented in a humorous and epic tone.

An advertisement for Dove body wash features women being interviewed about their cleaning habits. The ad then shows text graphics asking "Do you take care of your knees, elbows, and ankles?" - which cuts to video footage of young women saying no and shaking their heads in the negative. A slow-motion montage highlights the women using the body wash in the bathroom, while product packaging and branding are shown. The ad promotes Dove as a healthy body-washing product and is presented in an upbeat tone for a health-centric audience; and for this ad, specifically for women.

An advertisement for Kraft Macaroni & Cheese shows a mom and dad arguing about the lack of preparation for dinner while a boy addresses the camera while sitting next to a Southeast Asian man in a suit on the couch. The boy claims the dad brought his client home unannounced, and consequently, the mother didn't have enough time to make dinner, but managed to save the day by cooking Kraft Mac and Cheese. The ad promotes Kraft Mac & Cheese as quick and easy to make in case of an emergency, and is presented in a comedic and quirky tone.

A vintage Calgon laundry detergent ad targeted at housewives. The advertisement begins with a woman picking up her laundry from an Asian cleaner. She asks him for his secret to clean laundry, which he claims is an "ancient Chinese secret." The Asian wife enters the scene and reveals the real secret is Calgon detergent, and explains its unique properties by way of demonstration over a washing machine. As the customer leaves, the wife shouts, "We need more Calgon!", revealing the secret to the customer. The ad humorously highlights Calgon's superior cleaning power due to its ingredients.

An advertisement for Virgin Mobile shows a man and woman in an elevator while the man leers at the woman's body and inquires if she's there for a job interview. The elevator door opens, and he sees his boss and exclaims that he thinks the woman is sexy, just before the woman greets the boss as her father. Text graphics promoting Virgin Mobile appear over a shot of the man holding a box of his supplies after getting fired. The ad is presented in a comedic tone.

An advertisement for Netflix featuring Ricky Gervais watching his favorite shows and realizing how we would love to be a character in them. He steps into the shows and interacts with iconic characters from House of Cards, Lillyhammer, and Orange is the New Black, where they all remark that he doesn't belong in their respective shows. Then Ricky returns to his couch, suggesting it's best to sit back and watch Netflix on TV instead. The ad emphasizes the ease, convenience, and uniqueness of streaming Netflix original shows.

An advertisement for Arnold's Shapes biscuits shows a young man studying in an upstairs room while his friends send up a drone with the biscuits. He excitedly sees the drone and eats the Shapes as they are fired at him, culminating in the Shapes' branding overlaid on screen, before cutting to the drone firing Shapes at other residents on the apartment balconies. The ad promotes shapes as a shareable snack and is presented in a humorous and lighthearted tone.

A film trailer for Dirty Grandpa follows a young man, Zach Efron, and his grandfather, Robert DeNiro on Spring Break in Daytona Beach. After meeting a young woman, played by Audrey Plaza, they discover a world of partying and fun. The trailer shows engaging in golf, hanging out at the beach, partying in bars, and attending beach parties. It highlights the idea that we always have another chance at life and fun. The tone is playful, raunchy, and humorous, appealing to heterosexual young men and adults.

An advertisement for Disney Friends, a public service announcement against bullying. The main cast of several of Disney Channel's live-action sitcoms address the camera to challenge the audience to stand up and talk about bullying. Their talking points include "would you stand by and watch, would you say something, would you show courage?" Their call to action urges viewers to act and also log on to the Disney website to take action against cyber-bullying.

An advertisement for Prada Fall/Winter 2012 with fashion models that inhabit a modernist multi-level room covered in cream, red, and purple carpeting. The models are shown posing, walking, playing futuristic chess, and posing with chic handbags and sunglasses, showcasing the collection. It highlights what a woman should look like for the 2012 season and previews the collection up for sale. The tone is retro-futuristic and stylish, and the audience is high-end, fashionable women.

An advertisement for Nextel inventory management shows three middle-aged men dancing and listening to rap music in an office when a manager asks for the inventory. The music stops, and one man pulls his phone to inquire, relays the information to the manager, and resumes the dance party. The ad humorously highlights the ease of solving urgent business problems with Nextel’s service, targeting business customers.

An advertisement for clothing brand DC features a girl exploring a desert town in various DC-branded outfits and shoes. Upbeat music accompanies her adventure, showcasing a different outfit combination as the montage plays: her in her van, dancing, and running, all interspersed with close-ups highlighting the shoes and clothing, paying close attention to the "DC" branding logo. This ad emphasizes the versatility and the adventurous spirit of the girl.

An advertisement for Nestle Coffee Mate opens with a woman saying "Happy Anniversary" to her partner and hands him a cup of coffee. The man sits on a couch and drinks the coffee with a smile on his face. The woman tries to get his attention by dancing sensually in front of him, but the man continues drinking and ignores her. Then, the ad shows slow-motion footage of the coffee mate as a narration explains product details. The ad promotes the product with a humorous tone and emphasizes the irresistible taste of the product.

This Snickers advertisement shows teenage boys playing touch football in a park with Betty White. She gets tackled, resulting in an argument. They call her "Mike" and say she hasn't played well all day. A teenage girl walks over to "Mike" and hands her a Snickers bar, resulting in Mike reverting to his original form, a young man. The ad then cuts to a screen with the tagline "You're not you when you're hungry." A visual of a Snickers bar with the text snickers satisfies under it.

An advertisement for North Memorial Clinic promotes accessible healthcare services using clean graphics and mid-tempo techno ambient music. The video opens with the clinic's logo and reassuring text stating North Memorial Clinic "has you covered." Infographics highlight over 16 clinic locations, nurse triage, online scheduling, and additional online tools. Messaging emphasizes 24/7 availability via text, chat, email, or phone. Visuals shift to appointment options, including walk-ins and same-day visits. The ad concludes with its branding and contact information, encouraging booking an appointment today.

An advertisement for Connecticut Honda Dealers showcases scenic images of Connecticut as a narrator explains Connecticut's way of life and values. The ad features cinematic shots of cities, people rowing on a river, children riding in cars, and a Honda traveling on snowy, backcountry roads. The ad highlights how people from Connecticut are different, and are able persevere like a Honda Car.

An advertisement for Pocket Master shows a montage of video game footage of anime girls wearing (unofficial) Pokémon costumes while fighting or posing. Gameplay footage on a phone screen highlights its turn-based combat with chibi versions of the characters shooting magic at each other, while different match-ups of girl vs girl are overlaid. Upbeat music plays as the girls battle with magical powers before text branding appears. The ad promotes the game as action-packed and is presented in an upbeat tone.

A political campaign commercial for Lyndon B. Johnson features a little girl counting daisies in a field before voice over counts in reverse from from ten to zero. As the girl looks up, the camera pushes into an extreme close-up of her eye, and footage of a nuclear explosion is overlaid, with the voiceover explaining that "these are the stakes" if LBJ is not elected. The commercial promotes LBJ as a candidate who is anti-nuclear war and emphasizes the fear of nuclear disaster as a call to action. The commercial is presented in an ominous, warning tone.

This is a Pottery Barn Teen advertisement for the May Baby collection featuring Meg DeAngelis. The Ad has Meg and other teenage girls designing brightly colored home decor, then cuts to shots of them dancing in front of pillows, chairs, and artwork, showing them having a good time in a montage. Upbeat music plays as the woman dances and text graphics appear showing positive affirmations. The ad promotes Pottery Barn Teen as energetic, bubbly, and fun, and is shown in an upbeat tone.

An advertisement for Baileys Cream where a glass of falling ice transforms into a large group of women dancing on a round soundstage. The women are dressed in flowing Bailey's colors gowns as they perform synchronous movements, close-up shots of the dancers, and a woman diving off a tall ledge transforming back into a pour of Baileys. The ad highlights Bailey's as a social and fun drink presented in a visually stylized, energetic tone.

An advertisement for Subway features a blonde woman speaking in a child's voice to a nerdy man eating a Subway melt at his cubicle. She asks if he wants to be her boyfriend, and when he agrees, she swipes his Subway melt and walks away. A narrator says, "Get your own", while the sandwich is shown in its various permutations. The playful and fun tone of the ad highlights everyone's desire for a Subway melt.

This is an advertisement for M&M chocolate. The video opens with five M&M chocolates walking in from a garage door over Eminem's song "Not Afraid. The M&Ms then fumble over each other as the music changes to "Won't Back Down." The video then cuts to Eminem telling the camera, "This is what we do," before showing the M&M logo and its tagline, "can't resist," showing how irresistible M&M chocolates are.

This commercial promotes Motorola's Droid phone by parodying the style and format of Apple commercials. The commercial displays missing key features in iPhone via text starting with an "idont" tag, such as: "idont run widgets" or "idon't customize" while "Magic (oh oh oh)" by Mozella plays in the background. The tone is bright and cheery, mimicking Apple advertising, with the last tag line being "Everything idont". The ad suddenly glitches out to "Droid does" branding and a call to action to visit the "[droiddoes.com](http://droiddoes.com)" website. The commercial emphasizes the features of the Droid by pointing out that the iPhone lacks the very same features, promoting the Droid as the superior choice.

A candid video from a home recording of dolphins chasing a boat and repeatedly breaching by jumping above the waves. People cheer and whoop as the dolphins jump. The video is presented in a joyful tone.

An advertisement for TAC (Transport Accident Commission) shows two men ordering alcohol at a bar.
