First, their cups are full of drinks, then the bartender starts to pour their drinks out a few times as the narration reveals more information about the two men and their physical conditions, implying that they should not consume as much as they want to. This ad suggests that people know their drinking limits to avoid a transportation accident, emphasized by the ending tagline "Only a little bit over? You bloody idiot."

An advertisement for HP computers features rapper JAY-Z showing the functions of an HP computer. JAY-Z narrates the various tasks that he does on the computer while the video displays his hands interacting with CGI footage of holograms representing soundwaves, a chessboard, photographs, and maps showing his world tour. With the tagline "computer is personal again," the ad emphasizes how the computer can help with daily activities and highlights its high-quality technology, presented in a slick and futuristic tone.

This commercial is a PSA against drug driving. The PSA opens in a Chinese restaurant where a woman addresses the camera. She complains about customers under the influence and their resulting behavior, like being distracted and taking a long time to order. She questions how these people can drive while being on drugs, urging her customers to be careful while driving. The PSA then cuts to the customer walking out to the car as the tag line "Drug Driving Is it really that safe?" appears on screen, emphasizing that if someone can't even order food on drugs, then how can they drive safely?

This is an ad for "Yours Clothing UK", a female-centric, plus-sized clothing brand. It shows a variety of women enjoying themselves in social and personal situations while wearing fashion-oriented clothing. Key scenes show women in lingerie, bras, and underwear, feeling relaxed and proud of their bodies and style. The ad features the message that "fashion freedom is all yours," emphasizing that fashion isn't being gatekept by size standards anymore. The ad is presented in a light-hearted and groovy tone and uses a mixture of editing aesthetics.

An advertisement for Candy Crush Saga opens with an ice skater gliding across a rink before stopping when she notices a glowing purple gummy bear trapped beneath the ice. She puts on a ring labeled “King” and shoots a purple beam from her finger, melting the ice as the bear floats up inside a bubble. She pops the bubble and hugs the gummy bear. The ad cuts to a pink screen showing a phone with the game on it and the tagline “Release the Magic,” encouraging viewers to download the game for free.

An advertisement for The Dove Self-Esteem Fund shows a montage of young girls with accompanying text describing their insecurities regarding their physical appearance while an acapella version of Cyndi Lauper's "True Colors" plays. Text graphics appear saying "Let's make peace with beauty", while Dove branding is shown. The ad encourages girls to feel confident and that they are wrong about their insecurities, and is presented in an inspirational and uplifting tone.

This is a commercial promoting American Express via "The Ellen DeGeneres Show" that features Ellen having a day in her office. While doing the pre-show routine at the studio, she interacts with her staff and executives, all of whom happen to be animals. She passes by a turtle, talks to a writer elephant, a giraffe gaffer, an ostrich producer, and more animal staff while preparing for the show. Ellen narrates, "My life is far from ordinary, that's why I use American Express", emphasizing that the viewer chooses the card that matches their life the best.

An advertisement for Dick Smith's Aussie Grown Food shows Dick Smith himself advertising food products, such as sauces and spreads, on the basis that they are made in Australia. He stands in front of a row of Australian foods and flags and explains to the audience that other well-known brands are no longer Australian-owned -- intercut with quotes from other Australians that use sexual innuendo and off-color humor to support his products ("I love Dick"). Text branding and product packaging appear throughout the video as a marching band version of "Waltzing Matilda" is played. The ad has a patriotic (and somewhat bigoted) nature, of Dick Smith's products using Australian-style humor (and casual racism) to appeal to patriots, and is presented in a fast-paced, acerbic, humorous tone.

An advertisement for Citizen watches features Kelly Clarkson backstage delivering a narrated monologue. She walks onto the stage to a cheering audience. Then, a close-up shot displays the design of the product with a narration explaining the product features. This ad promotes this product in an uplifting tone and emphasizes that the product is powered by light, not by batteries. The ad ends with the Citizen logo and the slogan "BETTER STARTS NOW."

A Pantene shampoo advertisement shows a woman addressing the audience as she performs her haircare routine. She explains that her beautiful hair took effort, and with the help of Pantene vitamins, it strengthens the hair from the inside. She also remarks that her hair is healthy despite all she puts it through because of the product. The commercial highlights the effectiveness of the product and emphasizes a realistic approach to improving the quality of one's hair. The ad is presented in an informational and relatable tone, targeting women.

An advertisement for LEGO Star Wars: The Force Awakens video game shows a variety of humorous cutscenes over cinematic narration. The ad features a montage of LEGO characters engaging in incongruous behavior, including a LEGO man waking up in the desert with an alarm clock, a spaceship pilot having trouble with the spaceship that resembles car trouble, and a stormtrooper being hit with a helmet for messing with the lights. The ad parodies the original Star Wars Force Awakens trailer, highlighting the comedic tone of the game.

The commercial promotes Max New York Life's pension plan. It features a boy witnessing teenagers jumping into a river, contemplating the same, but he dismisses the thought due to his parents' disapproval. Now an adult, he faces disapproval from his boss, his pregnant wife, and his smiling kids when deciding to buy a car. As an elderly man, he jumps into the river he wanted to as a child with his gray-haired wife watching and encouraging him, emphasizing the importance of future decisions. A disclaimer graphic ends the commercial.

This is an animated commercial for the mobile app "Talk Life". The commercial features a teenager narrating their feelings of loneliness and lack of friends in a somber, morose tone. The app is discovered by the teenager, and suddenly the mood is bright and cheery, featuring the teenager messaging through the phone and finding people to talk to, emphasizing that the app can create new, fulfilling connections. The commercial ends with a title card "Talk Life" and spotlights the app's availability on different platforms.

An advertisement for the Taco Bell XXL Chalupa shows San Francisco Giants player Brian Wilson describing his idea for an advertisement for the product to a bewildered Director. The ad features him describing himself as a black ops soldier sneaking around and eating the XXL Chalupa and exclaiming that the product is "stacked." The ad highlights the size of the product and is presented in a humorous tone.

A concept video by Sonitdac imagines the features on the new iPhone. Cinematic music plays while displaying CG footage of the products from multiple angles and movements. It then shows a few camera modes in different scenarios and uses CG footage to showcase the intricate interior layout of the phone. This ad promotes the bold and creative concept by Sonitdac.

An Optimum Nutrition advertisement for Amino Energy features a muscular man describing his life as a sponsored athlete. He performs a variety of weight training exercises at a gym. The man's narration highlights the Amino Energy product as the necessary product for his athletic success. The ad is presented in a motivational tone for a fitness-conscious audience.

An NBA Store advertisement for BIG COLOR Christmas Day edition NBA uniforms. The ad features five NBA players representing different teams and uniform editions. The players synchronously dribble to the beat of "Carol of Bells." When their dribbles come to a halt, the instrumental plays under the narrator's voice as he promotes special edition Christmas Day Uniforms available at NBA stores and other retailers. The commercial emphasizes the NBA's participation in the holiday spirit and festivities.

An advertisement for Amul shows a montage of people in a wide variety of situations eating Amul products and enjoying them, including children at a party, a family at dinner, a couple at a lake, and military officers. The ad features a song promoting the brand as "the taste of India," emphasizing its connection to Indian culture. The ad is presented in an upbeat tone.

A political advertisement for John McCain opens with a clip of McCain delivering a speech about unity, perseverance, and American values. The ad transitions to a voiceover listing his political achievements while visuals highlight themes of service, leadership, and patriotism. It then cuts to archival footage from McCain’s time in the Navy, showing him answering questions about his Naval record while bedridden. The commercial ends with bold on-screen text featuring McCain’s name and the tagline, “An American President the American people have been waiting for.”

An advertisement for UCB Bank shows a montage of people in a variety of situations invoking the name of cricketer Sakib al Hasan. The ad features a wedding, a man in a workplace, and a maternity ward in a hospital where all the children are named after the player. Outside of the bank building, fans pose next to a life-sized cutout of Sakib as the real player comes out of the doors behind them, smiling. He takes photos with excited fans. It highlights the cricketer's immense popularity and associates it with UCB banking. The ad is presented in an upbeat tone.

An advertisement for Wayfair shows Peyton Lambton giving tips for decorating one's home. The tips include painting all the walls the same colour, sticking to one style for the entire house, sticking to one colour palette, and using complementary colours. It highlights the sale Wayfair is holding on its website, including free shipping for certain orders. The ad is presented in an upbeat, helpful tone.

An advertisement for Burger King shows a man interrupting his children who are playing with Hulk toys in order to mock the Hulk. The actual Hulk lands right next to the man, frightening him. It highlights the exclusive Burger King Hulk toy as well as the The Incredible Hulk film in theatres. The ad is presented in a humorous tone.

This is an advertisement for W by Worth. The video follows a woman walking through Williamsburg, Brooklyn. She exits the Bedford stop, buys bread and cheese at the Bedford Cheese Shop, and admires flower bouquets on sale on the curb. Her outfits change with each different montage as the ad ends with the tagline "Discover where style gets social," before changing to the logo W by Worth. The ad highlights the different outfits on offer. It's targeted towards a youthful, predominantly fashion-oriented female audience. The main slogan is "#WGOINGPLACES".

An advertisement for McDonald's features a young boy and a girl on a bench. The girl appears upset with the boy as emotional music plays. They spot a McDonald's across the street, and the ad cuts to footage of the Happy Price Menu, showing a close-up of the McAloo Tikki burger for just 25 RUB. The girl holds the burger joyfully and kisses the boy, who has his arm on her. The ad emphasizes the low price of the product and highlights its positive effect. It's targeted towards children.

An advertisement for Amazon.in begins with a man getting caught by his wife while taking food from the fridge and assuaging her anger by offering to buy her items on Amazon on his phone. The ad features a montage of people literally singing Amazon's praises, including a tourist couple, a family on a plane, a family at a dinner table, and more. It highlights the wide variety of products that Amazon provides. The ad is presented in a humorous tone.

This is a PSA by Women Rising featuring Lizzie, and several celebrities, actors, and athletes speaking out against bullying with clips of them saying, "I'm with Lizzie." The commercial brings awareness to the lack of a federal anti-bullying law, stressing that the viewer can stand together and lobby for the "Safe Schools Improvement Act". The PSA emphasizes that by doing so, they too can stand with Lizzie, an innocent victim of bullying, during National Bullying Prevention Month.

This advertisement for [VisitFlorida.com](http://VisitFlorida.com) promotes tourism in the state of Florida. It highlights various places and activities, like camping, visiting iconic towns, and rowing, while displaying fun facts on screen that might interest potential tourists. The commercial emphasizes all Florida has to offer, from unique places and adventures, encouraging visitors to explore them at "VisitFlorida.com."

An animated commercial for Bear Brand milk by Nestle features a sickly schoolgirl who recovers after drinking it. A catchy jingle highlights its benefits, while best practices appear at the bottom. The ad emphasizes Bear Brand milk's role in a healthy diet

An advertisement for PS4 shows two men instructing on how to share games with one another. One says, "This is how you share your games on PS4". A blue animated screen suggests a technical process, then abruptly cuts back to one man simply handing the game to the other. The ad emphasizes the ease of playing and sharing PS4 games.

This is a Buzzfeed infographic video highlighting various facts about different fast food products and chains. The facts are displayed in motion graphics style with green screen video of hands displaying different fast food chain items, as text displays the different facts while "Game Time" by Justin Cash plays in the background. The video promotes that there are more like it at the end, while having a call to action to subscribe and watch more of their videos.

This commercial showcases the Nixie, a wearable and flyable camera, in various scenarios. It captures moments like walking in a park, climbing a mountain, or biking in the forest. The commercial demonstrates the Nixie's versatility and highlights its power to offer a unique perspective, adding new meaning to everyday and special moments.

This is a commercial for Barbie dolls by the Mattel toy company. The commercial begins with the text, "What happens when girls are free to imagine they can be anything?" and proceeds to show little girls in positions of leadership in different environments. It shows little girls as professors for a college class, a veterinarian, and a soccer coach for a men's soccer team, among others. The commercial ends with a tagline, "When a girl plays with Barbie, she imagines everything she can become," and slogan "YOU CAN BE ANYTHING" over the Barbie logo.

This Gucci commercial is a fashion film featuring 20-something models running through a seemingly empty mall. The models led by a skateboarder are wearing prominently green, purple, and blue vintage Gucci-designed shirts, pants, dresses, shoes, and accessories. The models race to the rooftop of the mall to catch a sunset overlooking a city while "Goodbye Horses" by Garvey plays in the background. The fashion film emphasizes that Gucci, as a brand, is youthful and looking towards a hopeful future.

A PSA for anti-smoking shows a group of teenagers leaving school as an off-screen interviewer talks to one of the teenagers. The teenager stops and answers the interviewer's questions, revealing he once smoked cigarettes to try to be cool and fit in, but that he didn't like it and didn't need to continue trying to fit in. Text appears saying "Think. Don't Smoke." The ad promotes anti-smoking by getting a realistic response from a teenager that could be relatable to someone watching, and is presented in a documentary style and relaxed tone.

This advertisement is a teaser trailer for the Pixar Movie "Finding Dory." It features the regal tang fish "Dory" asking out loud, "Where is everyone?" and then reading the "Finding Dory" title card. After reading the title card, Dory ponders out loud that it sounds like a fun thing to do and proceeds to look for others to help "find Dory" while the song "Have you Seen Her" by The Chi-Lites plays in the background. The commercial promotes that the trailer is premiering on "The Ellen DeGeneres Show," emphasizing that the viewer will be going on a familiar Finding Nemo-like adventure when the film releases.

An advertisement from PETA parodies the tone of a pharmaceutical commercial to promote veganism. A woman wearing a neck brace and trench coat walks through the street as a narrator describes a fictional condition called “bwvaktboom,” jokingly explained as a side effect of a boyfriend going vegan, which results in better performance in bed. The ad cuts between her appearing injured and enjoying exaggerated aftereffects. She later arrives at her boyfriend's home, removing her trench coat to reveal her undergarments, and tossing him a bag of green vegetables. The commercial ends with a call to visit [**bwvaktboom.com**](http://bwvaktboom.com), suggesting the benefits of veganism are just a click away.

This commercial promotes the mobile game "Panda Pop". It opens with the tagline "Nobody Likes Sad Pandas" with a crying panda and features subsequent scenes of gameplay popping balloons next to overlaid onscreen text that says "SAVE BABY PANDAS" in sequential word order. The commercial ends with the "Panda Pop" title and a happy panda with the tag line "Be a Hero!", urging the player to be the baby panda's savior.

An advertisement for Cadbury's Dairy Milk shows a husband wearing a yellow shirt entering his living room, while his wife sits on the couch wearing a blue shirt. Initially rejecting his shirt choice, the man leaves upset. He returns moments later wearing a matching shirt to that of his wife they share the chocolate. The ad ends with a product image emphasizing its positive effect.

An advertisement for Specsavers features John Cleese struggling to start his car, leading to an exaggerated fit of comedic frustration. He grabs a tree branch and angrily hits what he believes is his own vehicle, only to reveal he is actually striking a nearby police car of similar color and shape. Officers step out to confront him, and Cleese runs away in panic. The ad ends with the tagline “Should’ve gone to Specsavers” and the company logo, highlighting the consequences of poor eyesight.

An anti-bullying PSA from [**bullying.org**](http://bullying.org) follows a red-haired boy during his after-school routine as he goes to retrieve his bike. A bully mocks him by calling him names and wearing a red hat to imitate his hair, while a group of teenagers looks on. The next day, the same scene begins, but one onlooker has dyed his hair red in solidarity. The bully notices and walks away, and the boy smiles. The PSA ends with a call to action and displays [**family.ca**](http://family.ca) and [**bullying.org**](http://bullying.org), emphasizing that standing up can be silent but visible.

This ad features a young boy in a car who receives a call on his car phone from a young-sounding woman asking him if he is, indeed, Burger King, and if he could deliver a chef's salad. Afterward, he receives a call from his dad, missing his opportunity to meet the pretty girl. The Burger King logo appears at the bottom with the tagline "SOMETIMES YOU'VE GOTTA BREAK THE RULES." The target audience is young adults who enjoy fast food.

This ad promotes BMC Security and Operations. It features a montage of corporate workers solving a problem, highlighting the tagline "Bring IT to life with BMC Advanced Security Operations." The ad targets tech/IT companies seeking cybersecurity solutions.

This ad is about the stock and commodities trading platform Nadex. The ad starts with a narrator voicing over an infographic saying that trading is as easy as saying yes or no with Nadex Binary Options. It then cuts to a screen with the Nadex logo, urging viewers that if they want to learn about the future of trading, they should visit [nadex.com](http://nadex.com). The target audience of this ad is new traders who do not have much experience and want an easy platform to trade on.

An advertisement for Allstate features Dean Winters as "Mayhem", who represents unexpected accidents and damage. First, he scratches a car's door heavily with a key in the garage. Then, he acts like a deer and appears in the middle of the road at night and gets hit by a car. Every time the accidents happen, the slogan "Mayhem is coming. Are you in Good Hands?" appears on the screen with cinematic music. This ad shows unpleasant situations that people can relate to, and suggests that Allstate can help cover sudden accidents.

This commercial for Nair hair removal gel features women dancing and singing to the jingle, "Who wears short shorts?" in a diner. They hold the Nair bottle as they perform a kick line dance, highlighting their smooth legs. The commercial promotes Nair's effectiveness in creating smooth skin for any occasion.

This vintage Coca-Cola commercial features various couples sharing a Coke in romantic scenarios. It ends with a montage of a couple kissing, followed by the Coca-Cola logo and the tagline "Coca-Cola is it". The target audience of this ad is young adults worldwide.

This is an advertisement for Bourn Vita Badam Booster. In the video, an Indian woman lectures to a group of parents in a bookstore. She speaks to them in Hindi as they listen and ask questions. The crowd asks questions, and the speaker answers regarding how Badam Booster helps kids get better grades. The music then swells as a kid drinks a cup of Badam Booster before it cuts to a pack shot on a white background, showing that this is a product for kids.

This ad promotes the gambling website [paddypower.com](http://paddypower.com). It features two men in a gym locker room. One man, Ben White, is recognized by another man in his underwear and abruptly embraces him. A man in a suit interrupts, claiming Paddy Power can't restore Ben's dignity but can refund his money with a special money-back offer. The ad ends with a close-up of the hugging men, accompanied by the Paddy Power website URL. Its target audience includes gamblers interested in online casinos.

The commercial for Centel's vehicle-based phone models shows a husband calling his wife from his Jeep. They check in on each other throughout his journey. He arrives at a dock, where his wife, revealed to have been talking to him on a boat phone, meets him. The tagline "Centel, Where people connect" appears over the boat continuing the journey, emphasizing Centel's ability to connect travelers.

An advertisement for Shopkins, a collection of kids' toys featuring five collections: the cupcake collection, cool & creamy, candy and cupcake queen collection. Each collection is shown being played with by a child's hand, with stop motion and characters animated to show the possibilities of play with each collection. It highlights the variety of fun activities there are with these toy collections. The tone is playful, and the target audience is aimed at young girls.

An advertisement for the Roadster Life Co. GTFO collection shows a man sitting in a dark apartment as a voiceover urges "get out." A montage depicts a woman waking up, riding a motorcycle with the man into an outdoor landscape, chasing after each other, embracing in front of a large fire on a campsite, and posing as day turns to night. The ad promotes Roadster Life Co. clothing for adventure seekers and outdoor enthusiasts, presented in a high-end cinematic style.

This advertisement for Turkish Delight features the candy being discovered among the dunes of an Arabian setting. A woman lies in wait in the desert, only to perish by the time a man finds her. The man digs through the sand and uncovers her body, whereupon he also finds Turkish delight on her person. The narrator highlights the ad's messaging by narrating the candy's slogan, "Try this Turkish delight, full of eastern promise," emphasizing that Turkish Delight is an all-encompassing experience that only its unique roots in the Orient can offer.

In an Expedia Hong Kong ([Expedia.com.hk](http://Expedia.com.hk)) ad, a young Asian man stands in front of a large computer screen, looking into the camera and pointing back at the site as he excitedly pitches vacation deals. The ad's storyline cuts through different scenes displayed behind him, like a travel montage, including a playful cutout airplane-window shot with an attractive woman behind him, plus a room filled with framed vacation photos and deal-style graphics. When the ad cuts wider, he’s already standing with two smiling women. The ad spot ends on a bright yellow [Expedia.com.hk](http://Expedia.com.hk) suitcase with the logo. The tone is wacky and irreverent.

An advertisement for LasikPlus shows a woman in a kitchen removing her contact lenses as she starts her day. The ad features her serving herself a bowl of cereal, only to realize instead served herself dog food, which was in a similar-looking container next to the dry cereal on the kitchen island. The ad highlights why the audience should consider LASIK eye surgery over regular contact lenses for better vision. The ad is presented in a straightforward, comical tone.

An advertisement for E Trade showing two men with a chimp in a suburban garage. The ad features the two men clapping along to a Mexican-style song while the chimp jumps up on a bucket to dance and clap along with the music. The monkey has a t-shirt that says e-trade. When the song ends, the screen reads, "Well, we just wasted $2,000,000, what are you doing with your money?" It highlights the idea that you can just blow 2 million as they did on the commercial, or invest your money with them. The tone is humorous, and the audience is for average middle-class investors.

An advertisement for the LEGO Star Wars II video game is presented in the style of a movie trailer. The ad features a humorous version of the rope-swinging scene from the original Star Wars, with Luke, Leia, and other characters attempting to swing across all at once before falling. It then shows a montage of cutscenes from the game, including LEGO X-wing fighters attacking the Death Star, Han Solo and Chewbacca flying the Millennium Falcon, and Rebel fighters battling walkers at a base. The ad highlights the game by showcasing its action-packed and lighthearted family-friendly gameplay.

An advertisement for WWE's Money in the Bank, a wrestling event where contestants compete for a briefcase with a world title contract. The ad shows wrestlers in a ring making for the briefcase, which is suspended above the ring. A montage features wrestling moves like pile drivers, ladder leaps, and flying tackles. The ad highlights the excitement and the need to purchase the Pay-Per-View, targeting young adult males.

An advertisement for Turbospoke through [Vat19.com](http://Vat19.com) shows an attachment that makes a bike sound similar to a motorbike. A voice-over explains how the product is a new and improved version of putting a playing card in the spoke of a bike, and footage is shown of an exhaust port-looking attachment on a bike and instructions on how to install it. A montage of young men doing jumps and tricks is shown. The ad highlights that, as a young adult, you can feel cool riding a bike that sounds like a motorcycle and is presented in an informative and lighthearted tone.

This ad is for the animal rights organization [peta.org.](http://peta.org) The ad starts with a man atop a podium delivering a speech to his club, the "American Kennel Club," discussing propositions to alter their dogs by "cropping their ears to maintain that clean look," when a man in a KKK outfit walks in. The man at the podium questions the KKK man's attendance, only to be left dumbfounded by the KKK man's rebuttal, as his beliefs and their beliefs are outwardly similar, which ends with the KKK man declaring that he is, indeed, in the right place. Then the scene cuts to a tagline which says "All dogs are created equal" and the call to action "Fight Breedism". The target audience of this ad is animal lovers who are against discrimination and dog cruelty.

In a texting and driving PSA, music plays as a young driver texts while riding with friends and drifts into the wrong lane toward another car. The music abruptly stops as both cars freeze in place, and only the two drivers can move. They get out, and the other woman asks if she knew she was in the wrong lane, stressing that she has her babies in the car. The young driver admits she was texting her mom and thought she had time. They return to their cars, time unfreezes, and a loud crash is heard before it fades to black with “Don’t text and drive,” plus 1HOUR OPTICAL and News Channel 6 ABC (WJBF-TV).

A PSA for an anti-abuse campaign shows a woman getting ready in the mirror, while a man stands just outside herdoor going through her texts. She walks out, prompting him to criticize her outfit, which she changes out of into a new, more subdued conservative one in shame. When she steps out again, the man blocks her path and commands her not to make a fool of herself, before a male voice-over states, "Abuse in relationships isn't always physical." The PSA highlights different forms of abuse that people should be aware of, and is shown in a serious tone.

An advertisement for the Volkswagen Phaeton features a series of shadow puppet scenes created by hands forming intricate images. The ad shows hand shadows transforming from deer grazing at shrubs to swans floating on water, followed by cities emerging and later giving way to civilization with fences, horses, and trees. The visuals end with the tag line "Isn't it beautiful what hands can do," before a shadow hand reveals the Volkswagen Phaeton. The video highlights the notion of the incredible things skilled handiwork is capable of, likening that sentiment to the craftsmanship of Volkswagen cars.

In an ad for Nike, Ronaldinho and his teammates keep the ball in play using mostly their feet, tapping quick passes as they move through the airport. They play straight through the checkpoint area, weaving between stanchions, lines, and security screening while onlookers stop to watch, backed by “Mas Que Nada” by Tamba Trio. The action briefly moves onto the tarmac outside, with someone watching from the airplane window, before the game continues inside again. A final kick clips a line-divider pole and misses the goal. The spot ends on the Nike durability logo, then Ronaldinho holds his head in disappointment. The ad highlights the active, larger-than-life feeling that Nike products offer.

An advertisement for Worth, a New York retailer, shows a montage of women in luxury clothing trying on and posing in luxury garments. The ad features close-up shots of a woman buttoning a sleeve, a black slit skirt, and groups of two women posing, walking, and sitting looking at the camera in different outfits. Text overlays suggest the experience of shopping there, i.e., shop luxury, on your terms, one on one, and fashion gets personal. The ad highlights that it is the place to get personalized luxury shopping in New York, targeted towards wealthy, white women.

A PSA for anti-smoking shows a pig's lungs on a breathing machine in a laboratory as cigarettes are fed through the lungs. The lungs darken and become discolored before showing a man cutting open the lungs, revealing the black, unhealthy interior, compared to a healthy set of lungs. The PSA shows the negative effects of smoking viscerally and grotesquely to promote anti-smoking and scare the viewer, and is shown in a serious and informative tone.

This ad promotes Sabritas by highlighting the prominent Brazilian soccer player Neymar. The ad shows Neymar boasting his soccer skills at a local park while holding a pack of Sabritas chips, garnering the attention and admiration of onlookers. It highlights the deliciously addictive nature of Sabritas to all those who enjoy them. The ad targets Neymar's fans as the main demographic, predominantly young men and boys.

A cinematic trailer for the mobile game Subway Surfers opens with a young boy hiding behind bushes near railway tracks as a train passes in the background. He looks both ways as a grumpy inspector and his dog walks by, narrowly missing him. The boy reemerges with friends, jumping into the air against saturated, multicolored rays before scattering. The cutscene shifts to gameplay as he spray-paints a train and is discovered, launching a chase through outdoor and indoor railways where he dodges obstacles, collects coins, rides a hoverboard, and travels atop moving trains. The trailer highlights the game's upbeat tone and the fun on offer.

An advertisement for Tacks ice hockey skates showcases the different iterations of the skates throughout the years. The different eras of the skates are superimposed over  NHL players, their player numbers, and the specific model of skates they've used professionally. The ad highlights the main benefits the skates offer for hockey players and the edge it grants them in a professional setting. It ends with a picture of the skates as well as a tagline "WE WILL WRITE HISTORY AGAIN", with just below the Tacks logo and the slogan "THE LEGEND IS BACK".

This segment from the daytime talk show "Ellen" features a commercial for the local mall, "East Hills," promoting their Back to School season. Local St. Joseph residents sign about stores and products in a campy, amateur tone. Ellen then reveals she hires those same residents to promote her Ellen merchandise store. The segment highlights a locally made commercial while also advertising the Ellen merchandise store in a down-to-earth tone.

An advertisement for Apple shows a black-and-white montage of archival images featuring figures such as Albert Einstein, John Lennon, Muhammad Ali, Winston Churchill, Martin Luther King Jr., and Mahatma Gandhi. The ad features scenes of these individuals thinking, speaking, and leading while a narrator reflects on how they were viewed as different or misunderstood. It highlights the idea of valuing people who challenge conventional thinking and believe they can change the world, over soft piano music presented in an inspirational, uplifting tone. It ends with the Apple slogan "Think different." under the old Apple logo.

An advertisement for the WWE Immortals mobile video game features WWE Divas, the Bella Twins, standing side-by-side as they both play the game and boast its features. A quick montage highlights the characters and their respective gameplay. The ad highlights the game's competitive gameplay and engaging action.

An advertisement for Trident Layers gum shows a father returning home and offering to pay the babysitter with a piece of the gum. The ad features the family gathered in the living room, joined by other people such as the mail carrier, chimney sweep, and electrician, all reacting enthusiastically to the gum. The ad highlights the layers of flavors in Trident Layers gum and the joy it brings when trying one. The ad is presented in a lighthearted, humorous tone.

An advertisement for Thai Life insurance depicts a father and son's life from childhood to adulthood, and how they grapple with the absence of the mother from their lives. Scenes include sharing meals, walking to school, learning to ride a bike, and the conflict over the son's desired music career, leading to his banishment by his father. The final scene shows the father in a car crash, with an alternate, happier life flashing before his eyes. The ad emphasizes life insurance as a way to care for loved ones even after death, with a somber, tragic, melancholic tone.

An advertisement for Vita Coco water shows a couple in front of a TV being asked by the narrator if they want to be healthy. The ad features a montage of all the health ads and diets they can try for being healthy, including the no-carbs diet, only carbs diet, hiccups diet, super-foods, hydration, etc. It points out how absurd and confusing all these suggestions can be. Finally, it suggests you can just drink Vita Coco water. The ad highlights how simple and healthy it is just to drink Vita Coco water if you want to be healthy and skip all the fads and diets. The tone is humorous and silly and is meant for a health-conscious consumer.

An advertisement for the Mobile Strike video game shows a military war room full of generals and soldiers watching a holographic table showing a virtual battlefield. The generals argue, worried at the carnage on the battlefield, until a high-ranking general steps into the war room, revealed to be Arnold Schwarzenegger. He takes a cell phone out of a locked safe and instructs the team to incorporate a defensive playstyle as he presses buttons on the smartphone, leading to victory as the enemies on the battlefield explode and run away. The video highlights the immersive quality of the game and the action-packed nature of commanding the battles, and is presented in a cinematic tone similar to an action film.

This is a commercial for the Wisconsin State Lottery promoting the "Mega Bucks Lightning Ball" variation of the game. The narrator says, " There is a cool new spin...." and goes on to explain the new lottery game. The commercial features different people spinning Wisconsin-themed signs, with graphics of lottery tickets and text explaining the new chances of winning the current game. The commercial emphasizes that the current game will only last for a short time and encourages the viewer to try their hand at playing and potentially winning.

In an ad for The Late Late Show with James Corden, James Corden sits in the front passenger seat while Candace Payne drives and J.J. Abrams rides in the back. The dash-cam framing keeps the moment casual, with humor driven by timing and reactions as Payne makes Chewbacca-style sounds. By the end, all three put on Chewbacca masks. The clip closes with on-screen promo text for The Late Late Show with James Corden and “Weeknights.”

A vintage advertisement from the 1960s by the American Tobacco Company opens with a Montclair cigarette pack and a cigarette with smoke swirling on an ashtray. A cigarette with the words CHARCOAL, MENTHOL circles around a cigarette stick, the word "MENTHOL" flowing out of a cigarette emphasizes their new charcoal menthol filter, which makes the cigarettes high in menthol, low in tar and nicotine. The ad persuades the viewer, flashing the word "SMOKE" several times on screen, with a male voice over saying "modern" Just enough in every puff. Makes every puff a pleasure," and a couple, with just their hands shown, share a pack of cigarettes.

An advertisement for K-Swiss footwear shows a fit man, identified as MMA champion Uriah Faber, jumping rope shirtless in a boxing gym. The ad features another man approaching him, incorrectly counting his jumps and mockingly commenting on how the shoe's tube design is compressed when he lands. When Uriah taunts him to try it himself, the man declines, dismissing jumping as not real exercise, and he walks away talking about "getting his swole on". The ad highlights the Tubes' sole technology as a distinctive feature designed to perform well during athletic activity.

This is a commercial advertising the different options for education provided by Strayer University. The commercial features a working mom promoting that Strayer University accommodates her schedule, intercutting footage from her daily life and her interactions with her campus, both online and in person. The commercial ends with the title card featuring "Strayer University" and the different programs it offers, emphasizing options for undergraduate, graduate, and post-graduate education.

An advertisement for Groupon with Timothy Hutton narrating about the plight of Tibet as scenes of Tibet, the Himalayas, and its people are shown before it transitions to Hutton sitting at a dining table at Himilayan Restaurant being served by a Tibetan man. He then tells you why, with 200 people buying the Groupon, you can eat at Himalaya restaurants for half the price. The ad highlights how Groupon offers discounted experiences through group purchasing. The tone begins seriously, only to shift to a subversive, lighthearted tone.

This is an ad promoting the Dazed magazine featuring Kendall Jenner as a part of #dazed100. The commercial opens with narration by Kendall Jenner saying, "Let it out, honey, put it in the book," and then features her saying disparaging comments about Kendall Jenner and intercuts with different footage of Kendall writing the same disparaging comments in a featured notebook. She does this in a hyper-stylized teenage girl's bedroom featuring excessive accents of pink and purple. The commercial emphasizes that Kendall Jenner deals with hyper-visibility by taking ownership of it and putting the negativity in a burn book.

An advertisement for Tropicana Frutz features a split-screen format showing a man and a woman going about their day: biking, working at a cafe, playing in the street, and converging in a bar where they enjoy a Frutz. The ad highlights the drink's freshness, vibrancy, and youthful appeal, mirroring the people who enjoy it. The one is energetic and youthful.

An advertisement for Nike football features professional soccer players in a van outside a museum, about to execute a heist. Inside, they steal a soccer ball guarded by lasers and samurai-like statues. The ad highlights Nike's sports equipment's unbeatable performance, with a high-octane action-movie tone that targets male sports enthusiasts, especially soccer fans.

An advertisement for a Limca drink shows a young man as he walks past a woman who catches his eye as he pursues her through a city. The ad begins with the man following her down the street as she sips from a Limca. She notices him, and as she sips from the Limca bottle, she gives him a flirtatous looks as she rushes through a glass pane that shatters into water in slow-motion before she descends on the elevator. The man gives chase inside the mall, up escalators, and finally into the streets again, where he takes a sip from a Limca and proceeds to step into oncoming traffic and in front of a car that also transmorphs into water. By the end, both the man and woman are left wet, finally enjoying the Limca together while laughing and standing shoulder to shoulder. The ad highlights how energetic this drink makes you feel and is presented in a playful, flirtatious tone aimed at a young, urban audience.

An advertisement for Dr. Fixit shows actor Amitabh Bachchan speaking to the camera from inside a cross-section of a house with water-damaged walls. His room of the house is connected on all sides to other rooms in a cross-section that shows different people leaking water and damaging his walls by showering, watering plants, and having parties, with his lighting fixture eventually falling from the ceiling. The scene then cuts to him talking from a newly fixed house that is in pristine condition, before branding and product packaging are shown. The ad highlights the excellence of the product, showing that it can be used for all types of repair, and it is presented in an informative and humorous tone.

An animated advertisement in the style of whiteboard drawings for [DefensiveDriving.com](http://DefensiveDriving.com) shows an animated character accessing the website and enjoying it. The storyline includes the main animated character sitting in a destitute classroom with bars on its windows before entering the world of the website, portrayed as a poolside resort. The ad features a narrator explaining that [DefensiveDriving.com](http://DefensiveDriving.com) is enjoyable in contrast to in-person driving school. It highlights the accessibility of the website, with the wide variety of platforms it can be accessed from, and the virtues of the course, including its A+ rating, insurance discounts, and state approval. The ad is presented in an upbeat tone.

In a Subway commercial, six young women in summer outfits dance into a studio set with wood-paneled walls. Singing an upbeat jingle, they move toward a craft-services table. Midway, the ad briefly cuts to them singing directly to the camera in a suburban neighborhood before returning to the studio. They eat a Fritos Chicken Melt, shown in split-screen boxed closeups with the sandwich. The music stops, and the women discuss the sandwich until a male announcer in voice-over recording equipment (headphones, microphone with pop filter, and script stand) appears astride them, whereupon he narrates a description of the Fritos Chicken Melt on the actual set before the Subway logo appears with “Eat Fresh.”

An advertisement for the video game Clash of Clans, where an elf fends off invaders from atop a tower. The ad is set in a medieval fantasy setting, and features the elf shooting at giant gnomes, a balloon pirate, "hog riders" (invaders atop of pigs), and dragons that she fends off with her fire arrows. She gets engulfed in flames from the dragon before finally defeating all enemies. The ad emphasizes that the fun never ends and there's always a chance to get a better score.

An ad for Cadbury 5-Star chocolate, where a young black woman in valedictorian regalia steps on stage to deliver a college commencement address. The ad features her attempting to deliver a formal address, but whenever she tries to speak, her mouth contorts to a cartoonish degree and speaks for her. Finally, the voice takes over and delivers an all-out endorsement of the chocolate. She takes one out and bites into it, enjoying it, and ending on a purple background with the "Cadbury" logo and the slogan "Free the Joy" just below it. The ad highlights the tagline "obey your mouth, and you shall be set free", presenting the product in a humorous tone.

An advertisement for Brandon Honda shows John Marazzi, the owner, standing in his showroom as he displays the cars for sale. The ad features him going through all the Hondas in his immediate vicinity, giving a brief description of them and their listed price, and explaining why customers don't have to be great negotiators to get great prices on a 2016 Odyssey, 2016 CR-V, or 2016 Fit, finally emphasizing that they are number one for a reason. The ad highlights why this is a good place to get the best prices on Honda cars in Florida, thanks to the generous offers and financing options available. The ad ends with the "Brandon Honda" logo at the top edge of the frame, an award for "2015 DEALER OF THE YEAR HONDA | FLORIDA" in the middle of the frame, the phone number "813.414.5406" in yellow lettering just above the web link for "BrandonHonda.com" in blue font, and an image of John Marazzi laying by the tailgate of a navy-blue pick-up truck with a dog, a doberman, to his right.

An advertisement for Wrigley's Double Mint gum about a young couple riding a Ferris wheel, where the young man tries to impress the girl. The ad features the young man fogging the glass and drawing a heart, and when he turns around, she is gagging on the floor from his bad breath. Wrigley's Double Mint gum is then shown, whereupon he takes two before the girl gets off the floor, relieved, and he fogs the window again to draw a heart that frames both of them. The ad highlights that if you want to be ready for all the important moments, you should always use Double Mint to be ready with longer-lasting fresh breath.

An advertisement for Snickers shows a group of people pushing a 4x4 truck along a forest-covered road with one guy at the wheel steering it. A woman in a shiny sequin dress and done-up hair stops pushing the 4x4 and exclaims displeasure, to which one of the men responds by offering her a Snickers bar. Upon eating the Snickers bar, she reverts to her original form, their male friend, implying his hunger pangs made him turn into a literal stuck-up drama queen. The ad presents Snickers as the solution to hunger-based displeasure. The ad ends with a graphic showcasing a Snickers bar with all its layers and branding.

In an ad for [realestate.com.au](http://realestate.com.au), Arnold Schwarzenegger sits across from a real estate agent in a busy coffee shop, scrolling Australian real estate listings on his mobile app. The agent follows along on an iPad, but Arnold leads the conversation, naming where he wants properties and directing the search. Arnold claims "Austria is the lucky country", to which the real estate agent gives him a hesitant look, then takes a loud, self-assured slurp of coffee, followed by a satisfied “ahhh.” The ad closes on “[realestate.com.au](http://realestate.com.au)” and “Australia lives here.”

In a Dove ad set in a minimalist white studio, women of different ages stand confidently in a bright, clean space with natural styling and simple, elegant clothing. The ad begins with a white background under the text "In a country of 631 million women there's so much beauty to be admired" and the Dove logo above it. Many appear to be of Indian descent, and a few wear a bindi, adding subtle cultural detail within the modern setting. The mood is calm and empowering, supported by soft, uplifting music. One shot shows a group of women hugging, emphasizing togetherness and support. On-screen text reinforces Dove’s message about real beauty and confidence, ending with the Dove name and logo.

An advertisement about the Toyota production system and how it helps manufacturers streamline their production and keep their companies running in America. The ad begins with an anecdote from ACE Metal Crafts as they relay the story of how they had fallen behind on deliveries to their customers, and how Toyota helped them streamline production so they could keep their company afloat. The ad states that a lot more manufacturing companies are leaning toward outsourcing despite 12 million Americans being employed in this line of business. The ad targets smaller manufacturing companies that are based in the US that need help with scaling their production.

This advertisement for Air Action Vigorsol chewing gum shows the cooling effects of the gum. A man on a beach takes out the gum and proceeds to chew on a piece. Upon consuming it, the man's nipples become comically erect, causing beautiful women around him to stare and give favorable attention. The man goes about his day with his nipples interacting with different objects and people, such as a rhythmic fence tapping, scratching turntables at a DJ booth, and catching a frisbee. The man's night ends with him in an elevator, offering a piece of gum to a beautiful woman. The commercial emphasizes that Air Action Vigorsol makes you feel "cool" even if you look silly, which in turn makes you attractive to other people.

This commercial is for the video game World of Warcraft, featuring Chuck Norris. A narrator boasts about Chuck Norris's prowess as he demonstrates his martial moves in a white void. This is intercut with clips from  World of Warcraft, which highlights an in-game Chuck Norris avatar counterpart also performing martial arts moves against in-game enemies. The commercial ends with Chuck Norris asking, "What's your game?" The commercial promotes Chuck Norris as a new addition to the World of Warcraft world and emphasizes a new reason to join the game.

This commercial promotes the Sega Genesis by highlighting its "blast processing" feature by comparing its speed to a race car and the Super Nintendo to a slow truck. It intercuts clips from Sonic the Hedgehog with the race car speeding down a racetrack. The tagline "Welcome to the next level" emphasizes that choosing the Sega Genesis means jumping into the future of video games.

An Audi advertisement shows four distinct key rings being hung up. The ad highlights the brand qualities of its model vehicles, like "design, comfort, safety, and sportiness", finally making the Audi logo when all four key rings are strung up next to each other.

This is an advertisement for State Farm. The ad features a husband talking to "Jake from State Farm" on the phone in the middle of the night, only to be caught red-handed by his wife, who thinks the husband is talking to another woman. The ad highlights that State Farm is reliable 24/7.

This is a spot about Samsung phones S7 and the S7 edge. In the segment, the phones are shown getting wet to show that they are water resistant in up to five feet of water as explained by a person in a wetsuit seated by a swimming pool. The person dives into the swimming pool while holding the phone and swims. Footage is shown of this person recorded from underwater in the swimming pool on a Samsung phone. The messaging continues on about Samsung improving the phones' battery life and memory upgrade options to show how great the phones are despite tough competition, and the person tosses the phone in the swimming pool. The tone is informative.

This ad is for Guinness. A person dances around a very large glass of Guinness in the foreground that disappears and appears as the person waves their hand. Then the glass of Guinness is removed and another glass of Guinness placed in its spot by another person. The dancing person grabs hold of the glass and is about to take a sip but the frame freezes and the words There's No Time Like Guinness Time appear; messaging the excitement of the alcoholic beverage. The tone of the ad is uplifting.

This advertisement for Hawaiian Punch shows two cartoon characters interacting and playing with each other.
